<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">PART&nbsp;I</font></b><a name="Parti_153054"></a></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">ITEM 1.&#160;&#160;&#160; <u>BUSINESS</u></font></b><a name="Item1_Business_153055"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Unless the context otherwise
requires, &#147;we,&#148; &#147;us,&#148; &#147;our,&#148; and &#147;Company&#148; refer to the business of
Smurfit-Stone Container Enterprises,&nbsp;Inc. and its subsidiaries.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">GENERAL</font></u></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Smurfit-Stone Container Enterprises,&nbsp;Inc.
(SSCE), incorporated in Delaware in 2000, is one of the industry&#146;s leading
integrated manufacturers of paperboard and paper-based packaging in North
America, including containerboard and corrugated containers, and is one of the
world&#146;s largest paper recyclers.&#160; We have
a complete line of graphics capabilities for packaging.&#160; For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009,
our net sales were $5,574 million and our net income was $8 million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are a wholly-owned subsidiary of
Smurfit-Stone Container Corporation (Smurfit-Stone), a holding company with no
business operations of its own.&#160;
Smurfit-Stone conducts its business operations through us.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">BANKRUPTCY PROCEEDINGS</font></u></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Chapter 11 Bankruptcy Filings</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;26, 2009 (the Petition Date), we, Smurfit-Stone and our
U.S. and Canadian subsidiaries (collectively, the Debtors) filed a voluntary
petition (the Chapter 11 Petition) for relief under Chapter 11 of the United
States Bankruptcy Code (the Bankruptcy Code) in the United States Bankruptcy
Court in Wilmington, Delaware (the U.S. Court).&#160;
On the same day, our Canadian subsidiaries also filed to reorganize (the
Canadian Petition) under the Companies&#146; Creditors Arrangement Act (the CCAA) in
the Ontario Superior Court of Justice in Canada (the Canadian Court).&#160; Our </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">operations in Mexico and Asia and
certain U.S. and Canadian legal entities (the Non-Debtor Subsidiaries) were not
included in the filing and will continue to operate outside of the Chapter 11
process.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The filing of the Chapter&nbsp;11
Petition and the Canadian Petition constituted an event of default under our
debt obligations, and those debt obligations became automatically and
immediately due and payable, although any actions to enforce such payment
obligations were stayed as a result of the filing of the Chapter 11 Petition
and the Canadian Petition.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We, Smurfit-Stone and our U.S. and Canadian subsidiaries are currently
operating as &#147;debtors-in-possession&#148; under the jurisdiction of the U.S. Court
and Canadian Court (the Bankruptcy Courts) and in accordance with the
applicable provisions of the Bankruptcy Code and the CCAA.&#160; In general, the Debtors are authorized to
continue to operate as ongoing businesses, but may not engage in transactions
outside the ordinary course of business without the approval of the Bankruptcy
Courts.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Debtor-In-Possession (DIP) Financing</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In connection with filing the Chapter 11 Petition and the Canadian
Petition on the Petition Date, we, Smurfit-Stone and certain of our affiliates
filed a motion with the Bankruptcy Courts seeking approval to enter into a
Post-Petition Credit Agreement (the DIP Credit Agreement). Final approval of
the DIP Credit Agreement was granted by the U.S. Court on February&nbsp;23,
2009 and by the Canadian Court on February&nbsp;24, 2009.&#160; Amendments to the DIP Credit Agreement were
entered into on February&nbsp;25 and 27, 2009.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The DIP Credit Agreement, as amended, provided for borrowings up to an
aggregate committed amount of $750 million, consisting of a $400 million U.S.
term loan (U.S. DIP Term Loan) for borrowings by us; a $35 million Canadian
term loan (Canadian DIP Term Loan) for borrowings by Smurfit-Stone Container
Canada Inc. (SSC Canada); a $250 million U.S. revolving loan (U.S. DIP
Revolver) for borrowings by us and/or SSC Canada; and a $65 million Canadian
revolving loan (Canadian DIP Revolver) for borrowings by us and/or SSC Canada.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">3<a name="PB_3_120235_5335"></a></font></p>

<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>

</div>

<div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the DIP Credit Agreement, on January&nbsp;28,
2009, we borrowed $440 million, consisting of a $400 million U.S. DIP Term
Loan, a $35 million Canadian DIP Term loan and $5 million from the Canadian DIP
Revolver.&#160; In accordance with the terms of the DIP Credit
Agreement, on January&nbsp;28, 2009, we used U.S. DIP Term Loan proceeds of
$360 million, net of lenders&#146; fees of $40 million, and Canadian DIP Term Loan
proceeds of $30 million, net of lenders&#146; fees of $5 million, to terminate the
receivables securitization programs and repay all indebtedness outstanding of
$385 million and to pay other expenses of $1 million.&#160; In addition, other fees and expenses of $17
million related to the DIP Credit Agreement were paid for with proceeds of $5
million from the Canadian DIP Revolver and available cash.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The outstanding principal amount of the loans under the DIP Credit
Agreement, plus interest accrued and unpaid, were due and payable in full at
maturity, which was January&nbsp;28, 2010.&#160;
</font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2009, we made voluntary prepayments of $383 million
on the U.S. DIP Term Loan with available cash provided by operating activities.
In addition, during 2009, we repaid $17 million on the U.S. DIP Term Loan with
proceeds from property sales.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31,
2009, no borrowings were outstanding under the U.S. DIP Term Loan or the U.S.
DIP Revolver.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2009, we repaid $35 million
on the Canadian DIP Term Loan primarily with proceeds from property sales
including $27 million from the sale of our Canadian timberlands.&#160; In addition, during 2009, we repaid $5
million on the Canadian DIP Revolver. As of December&nbsp;31, 2009, no
borrowings were outstanding under the Canadian DIP Term Loan or the Canadian
DIP Revolver.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As all borrowings under the DIP
Credit Agreement were paid in full as of December&nbsp;31, 2009, we allowed the
DIP Credit Agreement to expire on the maturity date of January&nbsp;28, 2010.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Reorganization Process</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Bankruptcy Courts approved
payment of certain of our pre-petition obligations, including employee wages,
salaries and benefits, and the payment of vendors and other providers in the
ordinary course for goods received and services rendered subsequent to the
filing of the Chapter 11 Petition and Canadian Petition and other
business-related payments necessary to maintain&nbsp;the operation of our
business.&#160; We have retained legal and
financial professionals to advise us on the bankruptcy proceedings.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Immediately after filing the Chapter
11 Petition and Canadian Petition, we notified all known current or potential
creditors of the bankruptcy filings.&#160;
Subject to certain exceptions under the Bankruptcy Code and the CCAA,
our bankruptcy filings automatically enjoined, or stayed, the continuation of
any judicial or administrative proceedings or other actions against us or our
property to recover, collect or secure a claim arising prior to the filing of
the Chapter 11 Petition and Canadian Petition.&#160;
Thus, for example, most creditor actions to obtain possession of
property from us, or to create, perfect or enforce any lien against our
property, or to collect on monies owed or otherwise exercise rights or remedies
with respect to a pre-petition claim are enjoined unless and until the
Bankruptcy Courts lift the automatic stay.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As required by the Bankruptcy Code,
the United States Trustee for the District of Delaware (the U.S. Trustee)
appointed an official committee of unsecured creditors (the Creditors&#146;
Committee). The Creditors&#146; Committee and its legal representatives have a right
to be heard on all matters that come before the U.S. Court with respect to
us.&#160; A monitor was appointed by the
Canadian Court with respect to proceedings before the Canadian Court.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the Bankruptcy Code, the Debtors generally must assume
or reject pre-petition executory contracts, including but not limited to real
property leases, subject to the approval of the Bankruptcy Courts and certain
other conditions.&#160; In this context, &#147;assumption&#148;
means that we agree to perform our obligations and cure all existing defaults
under the contract or lease, and &#147;rejection&#148; means that we are relieved from
our obligations to perform further under the contract or lease, but are subject
to a pre-petition claim for damages for the breach thereof subject to certain
limitations.&#160; Any damages resulting from
rejection of executory contracts that are permitted to be recovered under the
Bankruptcy Code will be treated as liabilities subject to compromise unless
such claims were secured prior to the Petition Date.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Since the Petition Date, we received
approval from the Bankruptcy Courts to reject a number of leases and other
executory contracts of various types.&#160; We
are continuing to review all of our executory contracts </font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">4<a name="PB_4_120322_5796"></a></font></p>

<div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">and unexpired leases to determine
which additional contracts and leases we will reject. We expect that additional
liabilities subject to compromise will arise due to rejection of executory
contracts, including leases, and from the determination of the U.S. Court (or
agreement by parties in interest) of allowed claims for contingencies and other
disputed amounts.&#160; We also expect that
the assumption of additional executory contracts and unexpired leases will
convert certain of the liabilities shown on the accompanying consolidated
balance sheet as liabilities subject to compromise to liabilities not subject
to compromise.&#160; Due to the uncertain
nature of many of the potential claims, we cannot project the magnitude of such
claims with certainty.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June&nbsp;2009, the Bankruptcy Courts entered an order
establishing August&nbsp;28, 2009, as the bar date for potential creditors to
file claims.&nbsp; The bar date is the date by which certain claims against us
must be filed if the claimants wish to receive any distribution in the
bankruptcy cases. Proof of claim forms received after the bar date are
typically not eligible for consideration of recovery as part of our bankruptcy
cases.&#160; Creditors were notified of the
bar date and the requirement to file a proof of claim with the Bankruptcy
Courts.&#160; Differences between liability
amounts estimated by us and claims filed by creditors are being investigated
and, if necessary, the Bankruptcy Courts will make a final determination of the
allowable claim. The determination of how liabilities will ultimately be
treated cannot be made until the Bankruptcy Courts approve a plan of
reorganization. Accordingly, the ultimate amount or treatment of such
liabilities is not determinable at this time.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In September&nbsp;2009, the U.S.
Trustee denied a request by certain holders of Smurfit-Stone&#146;s common stock and
7% Series&nbsp;A Cumulative Exchangeable Redeemable Convertible Preferred Stock
(Preferred Stock) to form an official equity committee to represent the
interests of equity holders on matters before the U.S. Court. The equity
holders subsequently filed a motion for the appointment of an equity committee
with the U.S. Court.&#160; In December&nbsp;2009,
the U.S. Court entered an order denying the motion for an order appointing an
official committee of equity security holders.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Proposed Plan of
Reorganization and Exit Credit Facilities</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In order to successfully emerge from
bankruptcy, we must propose and obtain confirmation by the Bankruptcy Courts of
a plan of reorganization that satisfies the requirements of the Bankruptcy Code
and the CCAA.&#160; A plan of reorganization
would resolve our pre-petition obligations, set forth the revised capital
structure of the newly reorganized entity and provide for corporate governance
subsequent to our exit from bankruptcy.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the priority scheme
established by the Bankruptcy Code and the CCAA, unless creditors agree
otherwise, pre-petition liabilities and post-petition liabilities must be
satisfied in full before Smurfit-Stone stockholders are entitled to receive any
distribution or retain any property under a plan of reorganization.&#160; The ultimate recovery to creditors and/or
Smurfit-Stone&#146;s stockholders, if any, will not be determined until confirmation
of a plan or plans of reorganization. No assurance can be given as to what
values, if any, will be ascribed to each of these constituencies or what types
or amounts of distributions, if any, they would receive.&#160; Because of such possibilities, the value of
our liabilities and securities, including Smurfit-Stone&#146;s common stock, is
highly speculative.&#160; Appropriate caution
should be exercised with respect to existing and future investments in any of
our liabilities and/or securities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">The Proposed Plan of
Reorganization</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;1, 2009, the
Debtors filed their Joint Proposed Plan of Reorganization and Plan of
Compromise and Arrangement and Disclosure Statement with the U.S. Court. On December&nbsp;22,
2009, January&nbsp;27, 2010 and February&nbsp;4, 2010 the Debtors filed
amendments to the Proposed Plan of Reorganization (the Proposed Plan of
Reorganization) and to the Disclosure Statement.&#160; Key elements of the Proposed Plan of
Reorganization were as follows:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">we and
Smurfit-Stone would merge and become the reorganized company (Reorganized
Smurfit-Stone) that would be governed by a board of directors that will include
Patrick J. Moore, Smurfit-Stone&#146;s current Chairman and Chief Executive Officer,
Steven J. Klinger, Smurfit-Stone&#146;s current President and Chief Operating
Officer, and a number of independent directors, including a non-executive
chairman, to be selected by the Creditors&#146; Committee in consultation with the
Debtors;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">5<a name="PB_5_120341_2897"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">all of the
existing secured debt of the Debtors would be fully repaid with cash;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">substantially
all of the existing unsecured debt and claims against us, including all of the
outstanding unsecured senior notes, would be exchanged for common stock of the
Reorganized Smurfit-Stone, which would be traded on either the New York Stock
Exchange (NYSE) or the NASDAQ market, with holders of unsecured claims against
us of less than or equal to $10,000 entitled to receive payment of 100% of such
claims in cash, and eligible cash-out participants having the opportunity to
indicate on their ballot the percentage amount of their allowed claim they would
be willing to receive in cash in lieu of common stock;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">all of
Smurfit-Stone&#146;s existing equity securities would be cancelled and existing
shareholders of Smurfit-Stone&#146;s common and Preferred Stock would receive no
distribution on account of their shares;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">the assets
of the Canadian Debtors would be sold to a newly-formed Canadian subsidiary of
Reorganized Smurfit-Stone free and clear of existing claims, liens and
interests in exchange for (i)&nbsp;the repayment in cash of the secured debt
obligations of the Canadian Debtors, (ii)&nbsp;cash to the Canadian Debtors&#146;
unsecured creditors if they vote to accept the Proposed Plan of Reorganization
and (iii)&nbsp;the assumption of certain liabilities and obligations of the
Canadian Debtors; and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Reorganized
Smurfit-Stone and our newly-formed Canadian subsidiary would assume all of the
existing obligations under the qualified defined benefit pension plans in the
United States and Canada sponsored by the Debtors, as well as all of the
collective bargaining agreements in the United States and Canada between the
Debtors and their labor unions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Proposed Plan of Reorganization
will not become effective until certain conditions are satisfied or waived,
including: (i)&nbsp;entry of an order by the Bankruptcy Courts confirming the Proposed
Plan of Reorganization, (ii)&nbsp;all actions, documents and agreements
necessary to implement the Proposed Plan of Reorganization having been effected
or executed, (iii)&nbsp;access of the Debtors to funding under the exit credit
facility and (iv)&nbsp;specified claims of the Debtors&#146; secured lenders having
been paid in full pursuant to the Proposed Plan of Reorganization.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;14, 2010, the U.S.
Court granted approval to extend the Debtors&#146; exclusive right to file a plan of
reorganization to July&nbsp;21, 2010, and granted the Debtors&#146; approval to
solicit acceptance of a plan of reorganization until May&nbsp;21, 2011.&#160; If the Debtors&#146; exclusivity period lapses,
any party in interest would be able to file a plan of reorganization.&#160; In addition to being voted on by holders of
impaired claims and equity interests, a plan of reorganization must satisfy
certain requirements of the Bankruptcy Code and the CCAA and must be approved,
or confirmed, by the Bankruptcy Courts in order to become effective.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;29, 2010, the U.S.
Court approved the Debtors&#146; Disclosure Statement as containing adequate
information for the holders of impaired claims and equity interests, who are
entitled to vote to accept or reject the Debtors&#146; Proposed Plan of
Reorganization.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Bankruptcy Code requires the
U.S. Court, after appropriate notice, to hold a hearing on confirmation of a
plan of reorganization.&#160; The confirmation
hearing on the Proposed Plan of Reorganization is scheduled to begin on April&nbsp;14,
2010.&#160; The confirmation hearing may be
adjourned from time to time by the Bankruptcy Court without further notice
except for an announcement of the adjourned date made at the confirmation
hearing or any subsequent adjourned confirmation hearing. There can be no
assurance at this time that the Proposed Plan of Reorganization will be
confirmed by the Bankruptcy Courts or that any such plan will be implemented
successfully.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Exit Credit Facilities</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;14, 2010, the U.S.
Court entered an order authorizing the Debtors to (i)&nbsp;enter into an exit
term loan facility engagement and arrangement letter and fee letters, (ii)&nbsp;pay
associated fees and expenses and (iii)&nbsp;furnish related indemnities<b>.&#160; </b>&#160;On February&nbsp;1, 2010, we filed a motion
with the U.S. Court seeking approval to enter into a senior secured term loan
exit facility (Term Loan Facility).</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">6<a name="PB_6_120404_3020"></a></font></p>

<div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On February&nbsp;16,
2010, the U.S. Court granted the motion and authorized us, Smurfit-Stone and
certain of our affiliates to enter into the Term Loan Facility.&#160; On the same date, the U.S. Court also granted
our February&nbsp;3, 2010 motion seeking approval to enter into a commitment
letter and fee letters for an asset-based revolving credit facility (the ABL
Revolving Facility) (together with the Term Loan Facility, the Exit Credit
Facilities).&#160; Based on such approvals, on
February&nbsp;22, 2010, we, Smurfit-Stone and certain of our subsidiaries
entered into the Term Loan Facility that provides for an aggregate term loan
commitment of $1,200 million.&#160; In
addition, we entered into a commitment letter and related fee letters for the
ABL Revolving Facility with aggregate commitments of $650 million (including a
$100 million Canadian Tranche), which we expect to enter into prior to exiting
bankruptcy.&#160;&#160; The ABL Revolving Facility
will include a $150 million sub-limit for letters of credit.&#160; The commitments for the Term Loan Facility
and the ABL Revolving Facility will terminate on July&nbsp;16, 2010 unless our
emergence from bankruptcy and satisfaction of certain funding date conditions
under the Term Loan Facility and the ABL Revolving Facility occur on or prior
to such date, and the Term Loan Facility is funded.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are permitted, subject to obtaining lender commitments,
to add one or more incremental facilities to the Term Loan Facility in an
aggregate amount up to $400 million.&#160;
Each incremental facility is conditioned on (a)&nbsp;there existing no
defaults, (b)&nbsp;in the case of incremental term loans, such loans have a
final maturity no earlier than, and a weighted average life no shorter than,
the Term Loan Facility, and (c)&nbsp;after giving effect to one or more
incremental facilities, the consolidated senior secured leverage ratio shall be
less than 3.00 to 1.00.&#160; If the interest
rate spread applicable to any incremental facility exceeds the interest rate
spread applicable to the Term Loan Facility by more than 0.25%, then the
interest rate spread applicable to the Term Loan Facility will be increased to
equal the interest rate spread applicable to the incremental facility.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On the date we emerge from
bankruptcy, the Term Loan will be funded and borrowings are expected to be available under the ABL Revolving
Facility.<b>  </b>&#160;&#160;The proceeds of the borrowings under the Term
Loan Facility, together with available cash will be used to repay our
outstanding secured indebtedness under our pre-petition Credit Facility and pay
fees, costs and expenses of approximately $50 million related to and
contemplated by the Exit Credit Facilities and the Proposed Plan of
Reorganization. Borrowings under the ABL Revolver Facility will be available
for working capital purposes, capital expenditures, permitted acquisitions and
general corporate purposes.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The term loan (Term Loan) matures
six years from the funding date of the Term Loan Facility and is repayable in
equal quarterly installments of $3 million beginning on September&nbsp;30,
2010, with the balance payable at maturity.&#160;
Additionally, following the end of each fiscal year, varying percentages
of our excess cash flow, as defined in the Term Loan Facility, based on certain
agreed levels of secured leverage ratios, must be used to repay
outstanding&nbsp;principal amounts under the Term Loan.&#160; Subject to specified exceptions, the Term
Loan Facility will also require us to use the net proceeds of asset sales and
the net proceeds of the incurrence of indebtedness to repay outstanding
borrowings under the Term Loan Facility.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Term Loan will bear interest at
our option at a rate equal to: (A)&nbsp;3.75% plus the alternate base rate
(Term Loan ABR) defined as the greater of: (i)&nbsp;the U.S. prime rate, (ii)&nbsp;the
overnight federal funds rate plus 0.50%, or (iii)&nbsp;the one month adjusted
LIBOR rate plus 1.0%, provided that the Term Loan ABR shall never be lower than
3.00% per annum, or (B)&nbsp;the adjusted LIBOR rate plus 4.75%, provided that
the adjusted LIBOR rate shall never be lower than 2.00% per annum.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The ABL revolver loan (ABL Revolver)
will mature four years from the funding date of the ABL Revolving Facility. We
will have the option to borrow at a rate equal to: (A)&nbsp;the base rate,
defined as the greater of 2.50% plus:(i)&nbsp;the US Prime Rate, (ii)&nbsp;the
overnight federal funds rate plus 0.50% or (iii)&nbsp;LIBOR rate plus 1.0%, or (B)&nbsp;the
LIBOR rate plus 3.50% for the first 90 days then 3.25% thereafter. The rate
could be adjusted in the future from 3.25% to a rate as high as 3.75% based on
the average historical utilization under the ABL Revolving Facility.&#160;&#160; We would also pay either a 0.50% or 0.75% per
annum unused commitment fee based on the average historical utilization under
the ABL Revolving Facility.&#160; The ABL Revolving
Facility borrowings are subject to a borrowing base derived from a formula
based on certain eligible accounts receivable and inventory, less certain
reserves.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Borrowings under the Exit Credit Facilities will be guaranteed by us,
Smurfit-Stone and certain of our subsidiaries, and would be secured by first
priority liens and second priority liens on substantially all our presently
owned and hereafter acquired assets and those of each of our subsidiaries party
to the Exit Credit Facilities, subject to certain exceptions and permitted
liens.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Exit Credit Facilities contain affirmative and negative covenants
that impose restrictions on our financial and business operations and those of
certain of our subsidiaries, including their ability to incur indebtedness,
incur liens, make investments, sell assets, pay dividends or make
acquisitions.&#160; The Exit Credit Facilities
contain events of default customary for financings of this type.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Going Concern
Matters</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The consolidated financial
statements and related notes have been prepared assuming that we will continue
as a going concern, although our bankruptcy filings raise substantial doubt
about our ability to continue as a going concern. Our ability to continue as a
going concern is dependent on our ability to restructure our obligations in a
manner that allows us to obtain confirmation of a plan of reorganization by the
Bankruptcy Courts.&#160; The consolidated
financial statements do not include any adjustments related to the
recoverability and classification of recorded assets or to the amounts and
classification of liabilities or any other adjustments that might be necessary
should we be unable to continue as a going concern.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Financial Reporting
Considerations</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For periods subsequent to the
bankruptcy filings, we have applied the Financial Accounting Standards Board
(FASB) Accounting Standards Codification (ASC) 852, Reorganizations (ASC 852),
in preparing the consolidated financial statements.&#160; ASC 852 requires that the financial
statements distinguish transactions and events that are directly associated
with the reorganization from the ongoing operations of the business.&#160; Accordingly, certain revenues, expenses
(including professional fees), realized gains and losses and provisions for
losses that are realized or incurred in the bankruptcy proceedings have been
recorded in reorganization items in the consolidated statement of
operations.&#160; In addition, pre-petition
obligations that may be impacted by the bankruptcy reorganization process have
been classified on the consolidated balance sheet in liabilities subject to
compromise.&#160; These liabilities are
reported at the amounts expected to be allowed by the Bankruptcy Courts, even
if they may be settled for lesser or greater amounts.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Reorganization Items</font></i></p>

to the reorganization include fees associated with advisors to us, the
Creditors&#146; Committee and certain secured creditors.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the Proposed Plan of
Reorganization, interest expense on the unsecured senior notes subsequent to
the Petition Date would not be paid.&#160; As
a result, we concluded it is not probable that interest expense that was
accrued from the Petition Date through November&nbsp;30, 2009 would be an
allowed claim.&#160; In December&nbsp;2009, we
recorded income in reorganization items for the reversal of $163 million of
accrued post-petition unsecured interest expense in the consolidated statement
of operations.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Liabilities subject to compromise
represent pre-petition unsecured obligations that will be settled under a plan
of reorganization. Generally, actions to enforce or otherwise effect payment of
pre-Chapter 11 or CCAA liabilities are stayed.&#160;
Pre-petition liabilities that are subject to compromise are reported at
the amounts expected to be allowed, even if they may be settled for lesser or
greater amounts.&#160; These liabilities
represent the amounts expected to be allowed on known or potential claims to be
resolved through the Chapter 11 and CCAA process, and remain subject to future
adjustments arising from negotiated settlements, actions of the Bankruptcy
Courts, rejection of executory contracts and unexpired leases, the determination
as to the value of collateral securing the claims, proofs of claim, or other
events.&#160; Liabilities subject to
compromise also include certain items, such as qualified defined benefit
pension and retiree medical obligations that may be assumed under the Proposed
Plan of Reorganization, and as such, may be subsequently reclassified to
liabilities not subject to compromise.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Bankruptcy Courts approved
payment of certain pre-petition obligations, including employee wages, salaries
and benefits, and the payment of vendors and other providers in the ordinary
course for goods and services received after the filing of the Chapter 11
Petition and the Canadian Petition and other business-related payments
necessary to maintain the operation of our business. Obligations associated
with these matters are not classified as liabilities subject to compromise.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have rejected certain pre-petition executory contracts
and unexpired leases with respect to our operations with the approval of the
Bankruptcy Courts and may reject additional contracts or unexpired leases in
the future.&#160; Damages resulting from
rejection of executory contracts and unexpired leases are generally treated as
general unsecured claims and are classified as liabilities subject to
compromise.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">FINANCIAL INFORMATION
CONCERNING INDUSTRY SEGMENTS</font></u></b></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h6 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">PRODUCTS</font></u></b></h6>

<h6 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h6>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our operations
include 12 paper mills (10 located in the United States and two in Canada), 110
container plants (90 located in the United States, 14 in Canada, three in
Mexico, two in China and one in Puerto Rico), 29 reclamation plants located in
the United States and one lamination plant located in Canada.&#160; Also, we operate wood harvesting facilities
in Canada and the United States.&#160; Our
primary products include:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">containerboard;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">corrugated
containers;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">market pulp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">kraft paper;
and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">reclaimed
and brokered fiber.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We produce a full range of high
quality corrugated containers designed to protect, ship, store and display
products made to our customers&#146; merchandising and distribution
specifications.&#160; Corrugated containers
are sold to a broad range of manufacturers of consumer goods.&#160; Corrugated containers are used to transport
such diverse products as home appliances, electric motors, small machinery,
grocery products, produce, books and furniture.&#160;
We provide customers with innovative
packaging solutions to advertise and sell their products.&#160; In addition, we manufacture and sell a
variety of retail ready, point of purchase displays and a full line of
specialty products, including pizza boxes, corrugated clamshells for the food
industry, Cordeck&#174; recyclable pallets and custom die-cut boxes to display
packaged merchandise on the sales floor.&#160;
We also provide custom, proprietary and standard automated packaging
machines, offering customers turn-key installation, automation, line
integration and packaging solutions.&#160; Our
container plants serve local customers and large national accounts.&#160; Net sales of corrugated containers for 2009,
2008 and 2007 represented 71%, 63% and 60%, respectively, of our total net
sales.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our containerboard mills produce a
full line of containerboard, which is used primarily in the production of
corrugated packaging.&#160; We produced
3,395,000 tons of unbleached kraft linerboard, 794,000 tons of white top
linerboard and 1,844,000 tons of medium in 2009.&#160; Our containerboard mills and corrugated
container operations are highly integrated, with the majority of our
containerboard used internally by our corrugated container operations.&#160; In 2009, our corrugated container plants
consumed 4,406,000 tons of containerboard.&#160;
Net sales of containerboard to third parties for 2009, 2008 and 2007
represented 17%, 20% and 21%, respectively, of our total net sales.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our paper mills also produce market
pulp, solid bleached liner (SBL), kraft paper, and other specialty
products.&#160; We produce southern hardwood
pulp, bleached southern softwood pulp and fluff pulp, which are sold to
manufacturers of paper products, including specialty papers, as well as the
printing and writing sectors.&#160; Kraft
paper is used in numerous products, including consumer and industrial bags,
grocery and shopping bags, counter rolls, handle stock and refuse bags.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our reclamation operations procure
fiber resources for our paper mills as well as other producers.&#160; We operate 29 reclamation facilities that
collect, sort, grade and bale recovered paper.&#160;
We also collect aluminum and plastics for resale to manufacturers of
these products.&#160; In addition, we operate
a nationwide brokerage system whereby we purchase and resell recovered paper to
our recycled paper mills and other producers on a regional and national
contract basis.&#160; Our waste reduction
services extract additional recyclables from the waste stream by partnering
with customers to reduce their waste expenses and increase efficiencies.&#160; Brokerage contracts provide bulk purchasing,
often resulting in lower prices and cleaner recovered paper.&#160; Many of our reclamation facilities are
located close to our recycled paper mills, ensuring availability of supply with
minimal shipping costs.&#160; In 2009, our
paper mills consumed 1,952,000 tons of the fiber reclaimed and brokered by our
reclamation operations, representing an integration level of approximately 38%.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">10<a name="PB_10_120658_8146"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-decoration:underline;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">RAW MATERIALS</font></u></b></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Wood
fiber and reclaimed fiber are the principal raw materials used in the
manufacture of our paper products.&#160; We
satisfy the majority of our need for wood fiber through purchases on the open
market or under supply agreements.&#160; We
satisfy essentially all of our need for reclaimed fiber through our reclamation
facilities and nationwide brokerage system.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-decoration:underline;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">MARKETING AND DISTRIBUTION</font></u></b></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our marketing
strategy is to sell a broad range of paper-based packaging products to
manufacturers of industrial and consumer products.&#160; We seek to meet the quality and service needs
of the customers of our converting plants at the most efficient cost, while
balancing those needs against the demands of our open market paperboard
customers.&#160; Our converting plants focus
on supplying both specialized packaging with high value graphics that enhance a
product&#146;s market appeal and high-volume commodity products.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We serve a broad customer base.&#160; We serve thousands of accounts from our
plants and sell packaging and other products directly to end users and
converters, as well as through resellers.&#160;
Our corrugated container sales organization is centralized with sales
responsibilities for all converting plants.&#160;
This allows us to better focus on revenue growth and assign the
appropriate resources to the best opportunities. &#160;Marketing of containerboard and
pulp to third parties is centralized in our board sales group.&#160; Total tons of containerboard and
market pulp sold to third parties in 2009, 2008 and 2007 were 2,245,000,
3,024,000 and 3,381,000, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our business
is not dependent upon a single customer or upon a small number of major
customers.&#160; We do not believe the loss of
any one customer would have a material adverse effect on our business.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-decoration:underline;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COMPETITION</font></u></b></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
markets in which we sell our principal products are highly competitive and
comprised of many participants.&#160; Although
no single company is dominant, we do face significant competitors, including
large vertically integrated companies as well as numerous smaller
companies.&#160; The markets in which we
compete have historically been sensitive to price fluctuations brought about by
shifts in industry capacity and other cyclical industry conditions.&#160; While we compete primarily on the basis of
price in many of our product lines, other competitive factors include design,
quality and service, with varying emphasis depending on product line.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">BACKLOG</font></u></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Demand
for our major product lines is relatively constant throughout the year, and
seasonal fluctuations in marketing, production, shipments and inventories are
not significant.&#160; Backlog orders are not
a significant factor in the industry.&#160; We
do not have a significant backlog of orders as most orders are placed for
delivery within 30 days.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-decoration:underline;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">RESEARCH AND NEW PRODUCT
DEVELOPMENT</font></u></b></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
majority of our research and new product development activities are performed
at our facility located in Carol Stream, Illinois.&#160; We use advanced technology to assist all
levels of the manufacturing and sales processes, from raw material supply
through finished packaging performance.&#160;
Research programs have provided improvements in coatings and barriers,
stiffeners, inks and printing.&#160; Our
technical staff conducts basic, applied and diagnostic research, develops
processes and products and provides a wide range of other technical
services.&#160; In each of 2009, 2008 and
2007, we spent approximately $3 million on research and new product development
activities.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-decoration:underline;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY</font></u></b></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We
actively pursue applications for patents on new technologies and designs and
attempt to protect our patents against infringement.&#160; Nevertheless, we believe our success and
growth are more dependent on the quality of our products and our relationships
with customers than on the extent of our patent protection.&#160; We hold or are licensed to use certain
patents, licenses, trademarks and trade names on our products, but do not
consider the successful continuation of any material aspect of our business to
be dependent upon such intellectual property.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-decoration:underline;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">EMPLOYEES</font></u></b></p>

customary for the industry, the type of facility, the classification of the

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-decoration:underline;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ENVIRONMENTAL COMPLIANCE</font></u></b></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our
operations are subject to extensive environmental regulation by federal, state,
local and foreign authorities.&#160; In the
past, we have made significant capital expenditures to comply with water, air,
solid and hazardous waste and other environmental laws and regulations.&#160; We expect to make significant expenditures in
the future for environmental compliance.&#160;
Because various environmental standards are subject to change, it is
difficult to predict with certainty the amount of capital expenditures that
will ultimately be required to comply with future standards.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">12<a name="PB_12_121327_4141"></a></font></p>

<div>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of
Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The U.S. Congress and several states
in which we operate are considering legislation that would mandate the
reduction of greenhouse gas emissions from facilities in various sectors of the
economy, including manufacturing. The United States Environmental Protection
Agency (EPA) is also taking steps to regulate greenhouse gas emissions under
certain Clean Air Act programs.&#160;
Enactment of new climate change laws or regulations may require capital
expenditures to modify assets to meet greenhouse gas reduction requirements,
increase energy costs above the level of general inflation, and could result in
direct compliance and other costs.&#160; It is
not yet known when such greenhouse gas emission laws or regulations may come
into effect, nor is it currently possible to estimate the costs of compliance
with such laws or regulations.&#160; We have
taken voluntary actions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from our
manufacturing operations and, with our membership in the Chicago Climate
Exchange, have committed to reduce these emissions by 6% over baseline
(emissions from 1998 to 2001) by the end of 2010.&#160; We expect that we will not be
disproportionately affected by new climate change laws or regulations as
compared to our competitors who have comparable, energy-intensive operations in
the United States.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2004, EPA promulgated a Maximum
Achievable Control Technology (MACT) regulation to limit hazardous air
pollutant emissions from certain industrial boilers (Boiler MACT).&#160; Several of our mills were required to install
new pollution control equipment in order to meet the compliance deadline of September&nbsp;13,
2007.&#160; The Boiler<b>  </b>MACT rule&nbsp;was
challenged by third parties in litigation, and the United States District Court
of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit issued a decision vacating Boiler MACT and
remanding the rule&nbsp;to the EPA.&#160; All
projects required to bring us into compliance with the now vacated Boiler MACT
requirements were completed.&#160; We spent approximately $80 million on Boiler
MACT projects principally through 2007 with insignificant amounts spent in 2008
and 2009 as the project neared completion.&#160;
It is presently<b>  </b>unclear whether future rulemaking
will require us to install additional pollution control equipment on industrial
boilers at our facilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Excluding the spending on Boiler
MACT projects described above and other one-time compliance costs, for the past
three years we spent an average of approximately $4 million annually on capital
expenditures for environmental purposes. We anticipate additional capital
expenditures related to environmental compliance in the future.&#160; Since our principal competitors are subject
to comparable environmental standards, it is our opinion, based on current
information, that compliance with existing environmental standards should not
adversely affect our competitive position or operating results.&#160; However, we could incur significant
expenditures due to changes in law or the discovery of new information, which
could have a material adverse effect on our operating results.&#160; See Part&nbsp;I, Item 3. Legal Proceedings - &#147;Environmental
Matters.&#148;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-decoration:underline;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">EXECUTIVE OFFICERS OF THE
REGISTRANT</font></u></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">ITEM 1A.<a name="Item1a__121957"></a> <u>RISK
FACTORS</u></font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are subject to
certain risks and events that, if one or more of them occur, could adversely
affect our business, our financial condition and results of operations. You
should consider the following risk factors, in addition to the other
information presented in this report, as well as the other reports and
registration statements we file from time to time with the SEC, in evaluating
us, our business and an investment in our securities. The risks below are not
the only ones we face. Additional risks not currently known to us or that we
currently deem immaterial also may adversely impact our business.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Bankruptcy
Related Risk Factors</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">We filed for protection
under Chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code and our Canadian subsidiaries filed to
reorganize under the CCAA on January&nbsp;26, 2009.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During our
bankruptcy proceedings, our operations and our ability to execute our business
plan are subject to the risks and uncertainties associated with bankruptcy.
Risks and uncertainties associated with our bankruptcy proceedings include the
following:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .2in;text-indent:-.2in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our ability
to obtain court approval with respect to motions filed in the bankruptcy
proceedings from time to time;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .2in;text-indent:-.2in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our ability
to obtain confirmation and consummate our Proposed Plan of Reorganization with
respect to the bankruptcy proceedings;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .2in;text-indent:-.2in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our ability
to obtain and maintain commercially reasonable terms with vendors and service
providers;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .2in;text-indent:-.2in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our ability
to renew contracts that are critical to our operations;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .2in;text-indent:-.2in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our ability
to retain management and other key individuals;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .2in;text-indent:-.2in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There can be
no assurance that the Creditors&#146; Committee will support our positions on
matters to be presented to the Bankruptcy Courts in the future; and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .2in;text-indent:-.2in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Disagreements
between us and the Creditors&#146; Committee could protract the Chapter 11
proceedings, negatively impact our ability to operate and delay our emergence
from the Chapter 11 proceedings.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .2in;text-indent:-.2in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Objections
to the Plan of Reorganization could protract the Chapter 11 proceedings.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">These risks and uncertainties could
affect our business and operations in various ways. For example, negative
events or publicity associated with our bankruptcy proceedings could adversely
affect our sales and relationships with our customers, as well as with vendors
and employees, which in turn could adversely affect our operations and
financial condition, particularly if the bankruptcy proceedings are protracted.
Also, transactions outside the ordinary course of business are subject to the
prior approval of the Bankruptcy Courts, which may limit our ability to respond
timely to certain events or take advantage of certain opportunities.</font></p>
