<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></b><a name="NotesToConsolidatedFinancialState_140024"></a></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(Tabular amounts in millions)</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">1.&#160; Bankruptcy Proceedings</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Chapter
11 Bankruptcy Filings</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;26, 2009 (the &#147;Petition Date&#148;),
Smurfit-Stone Container Corporation (&#147;SSCC&#148;), Smurfit-Stone Container
Enterprises,&nbsp;Inc. (&#147;SSCE&#148; or the &#147;Company&#148;) and its U.S. and Canadian
subsidiaries (collectively, the &#147;Debtors&#148;) filed a voluntary petition (the &#147;Chapter
11 Petition&#148;) for relief under Chapter 11 of the United States Bankruptcy Code
(the &#147;Bankruptcy Code&#148;) in the United States Bankruptcy Court in Wilmington,
Delaware (the &#147;U.S. Court&#148;).&#160; On the same
day, the Company&#146;s Canadian subsidiaries also filed to reorganize (the &#147;Canadian
Petition&#148;) under the Companies&#146; Creditors Arrangement Act (the &#147;CCAA&#148;) in the
Ontario Superior Court of Justice in Canada (the &#147;Canadian Court&#148;).&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company&#146;s operations in Mexico and Asia and certain U.S. and Canadian legal
entities (the &#147;Non-Debtor Subsidiaries&#148;) were not included in the filing and
will continue to operate outside of the Chapter 11 process.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The filing
of the Chapter&nbsp;11 Petition and the Canadian Petition constituted an event
of default under the Company&#146;s debt obligations, and those debt obligations
became automatically and immediately due and payable, although any actions to
enforce such payment obligations were stayed as a result of the filing of the
Chapter 11 Petition and the Canadian Petition.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SSCC, the Company and its U.S. and Canadian
subsidiaries are currently operating as &#147;debtors-in-possession&#148; under the
jurisdiction of the U.S. Court and Canadian Court (the &#147;Bankruptcy Courts&#148;) and
in accordance with the applicable provisions of the Bankruptcy Code and the
CCAA.&#160; In general, the Debtors are
authorized to continue to operate as ongoing businesses, but may not engage in
transactions outside the ordinary course of business without the approval of
the Bankruptcy Courts.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Debtor-In-Possession (&#147;DIP&#148;) Financing</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In connection with filing the Chapter 11
Petition and the Canadian Petition on the Petition Date, the Company, SSCC and
certain of its affiliates filed a motion with the Bankruptcy Courts seeking
approval to enter into a Post-Petition Credit Agreement (the &#147;DIP Credit
Agreement&#148;). Final approval of the DIP Credit Agreement was granted by the U.S.
Court on February&nbsp;23, 2009 and by the Canadian Court on February&nbsp;24,
2009.&#160; Amendments to the DIP Credit
Agreement were entered into on February&nbsp;25 and 27, 2009.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The DIP Credit Agreement, as amended, provided
for borrowings up to an aggregate committed amount of $750 million, consisting
of a $400 million U.S. term loan (&#147;U.S. DIP Term Loan&#148;) for borrowings by the
Company; a $35 million Canadian term loan (&#147;Canadian DIP Term Loan&#148;) for
borrowings by Smurfit-Stone Container Canada Inc. (&#147;SSC Canada&#148;); a $250
million U.S. revolving loan (&#147;U.S. DIP Revolver&#148;) for borrowings by the Company
and/or SSC Canada; and a $65 million Canadian revolving loan (&#147;Canadian DIP
Revolver&#148;) for borrowings by the Company and/or SSC Canada.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the
DIP Credit Agreement, on January&nbsp;28, 2009, the Company borrowed $440
million, consisting of a $400 million U.S. DIP Term Loan, a $35 million Canadian
DIP Term loan and $5 million from the Canadian DIP Revolver.&#160; In accordance with the terms of the DIP Credit
Agreement, in January&nbsp;2009 the Company used U.S. DIP Term Loan proceeds of
$360 million, net of lenders&#146; fees of $40 million, and Canadian DIP Term Loan
proceeds of $30 million, net of lenders&#146; fees of $5 million, to terminate the
receivables securitization programs and repay all indebtedness outstanding
under the programs of $385 million and to pay other expenses of $1
million.&#160; In addition, other fees and
expenses of $17 million related to the DIP Credit Agreement were paid for with
proceeds of $5 million from the Canadian DIP Revolver and available cash.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">51<a name="PB_51_190153_7748"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The outstanding principal amount of the loans
under the DIP Credit Agreement, plus interest accrued and unpaid, were due and
payable in full at maturity, which was January&nbsp;28, 2010.&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During
2009, the Company made voluntary prepayments of $383 million on the U.S. DIP
Term Loan with available cash provided by operating activities. In addition,
the Company repaid $17 million on the U.S. DIP Term Loan with proceeds from
property sales.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31,
2009, no borrowings were outstanding under the U.S. DIP Term Loan or the U.S.
DIP Revolver.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During
2009, the Company repaid $35 million on the Canadian DIP Term Loan primarily
with proceeds from property sales, including $27 million from the sale of the
Company&#146;s Canadian timberlands.&#160; In
addition, during 2009, the Company repaid $5 million on the Canadian DIP
Revolver. As of December&nbsp;31, 2009, no borrowings were outstanding under
the Canadian DIP Term Loan or the Canadian DIP Revolver.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As all
borrowings under the DIP Credit Agreement were paid in full as of December&nbsp;31,
2009, the Company allowed the DIP Credit Agreement to expire on the maturity
date of January&nbsp;28, 2010 (See Note 9).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Reorganization
Process</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Bankruptcy Courts approved payment of certain of the Company&#146;s pre-petition
obligations, including employee wages, salaries and benefits, and the payment
of vendors and other providers in the ordinary course for goods received and
services rendered subsequent to the filing of the Chapter 11 Petition and
Canadian Petition and other business-related payments necessary to
maintain&nbsp;the operation of the Company&#146;s business.&#160; The Company retained legal and financial
professionals to advise it on the bankruptcy proceedings.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Immediately
after filing the Chapter 11 Petition and Canadian Petition, the Company
notified all known current or potential creditors of the bankruptcy
filings.&#160; Subject to certain exceptions
under the Bankruptcy Code and the CCAA, the Company&#146;s bankruptcy filings
automatically enjoined, or stayed, the continuation of any judicial or
administrative proceedings or other actions against the Company or its property
to recover, collect or secure a claim arising prior to the filing of the
Chapter 11 Petition and Canadian Petition.&#160;
Thus, for example, most creditor actions to obtain possession of
property from the Company, or to create, perfect or enforce any lien against
its property, or to collect on monies owed or otherwise exercise rights or
remedies with respect to a pre-petition claim are enjoined unless and until the
Bankruptcy Courts lift the automatic stay.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As
required by the Bankruptcy Code, the United States Trustee for the District of
Delaware (the &#147;U.S. Trustee&#148;) appointed an official committee of unsecured
creditors (the &#147;Creditors&#146; Committee&#148;). The Creditors&#146; Committee and its legal
representatives have a right to be heard on all matters that come before the
U.S. Court with respect to the Company.&#160;
A monitor was appointed by the Canadian Court with respect to
proceedings before the Canadian Court.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the Bankruptcy Code, the
Debtors generally must assume or reject pre-petition executory contracts,
including but not limited to real property leases, subject to the approval of
the Bankruptcy Courts and certain other conditions. &#160;In this context, &#147;assumption&#148; means that the
Company agrees to perform its obligations and cure all existing defaults under
the contract or lease, and &#147;rejection&#148; means that it is relieved from its
obligations to perform further under the contract or lease, but is subject to a
pre-petition claim for damages for the breach thereof subject to certain
limitations.&#160; Any damages resulting from
rejection of executory contracts that are permitted to be recovered under the Bankruptcy
Code will be treated as liabilities subject to compromise unless such claims
were secured prior to the Petition Date.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Since the
Petition Date, the Company received approval from the Bankruptcy Courts to
reject a number of leases and other executory contracts of various types.&#160; The Company is continuing to review all of
its executory contracts and unexpired leases to determine which additional
contracts and leases it will reject. </font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">52<a name="PB_52_190202_141"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of
Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company expects that additional liabilities subject to compromise will arise
due to rejection of executory contracts, including leases, and from the
determination of the U.S. Court (or agreement by parties in interest) of
allowed claims for contingencies and other disputed amounts.&#160; The Company also expects that the assumption
of additional executory contracts and unexpired leases will convert certain of
the liabilities shown on the accompanying consolidated balance sheet as
liabilities subject to compromise to liabilities not subject to
compromise.&#160; Due to the uncertain nature
of many of the potential claims, the Company cannot project the magnitude of
such claims with certainty.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June&nbsp;2009, the Bankruptcy
Courts entered an order establishing August&nbsp;28, 2009, as the bar date for
potential creditors to file claims.&nbsp; The bar date is the date by which
certain claims against the Company must be filed if the claimants wish to
receive any distribution in the bankruptcy cases. Proof of claim forms received
after the bar date are typically not eligible for consideration of recovery as
part of the Company&#146;s bankruptcy cases.&#160;
Creditors were notified of the bar date and the requirement to file a
proof of claim with the Bankruptcy Courts. Differences between liability
amounts estimated by the Company and claims filed by creditors are being
investigated and, if necessary, the Bankruptcy Courts will make a final
determination of the allowable claim. The determination of how liabilities will
ultimately be treated cannot be made until the Bankruptcy Courts approve a plan
of reorganization. Accordingly, the ultimate amount or treatment of such
liabilities is not determinable at this time.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In September&nbsp;2009,
the U.S. Trustee denied a request by certain holders of SSCC&#146;s common stock and
7% Series&nbsp;A Cumulative Exchangeable Redeemable Convertible Preferred Stock
(&#147;Preferred Stock&#148;) to form an official equity committee to represent the
interests of equity holders on matters before the U.S. Court. The equity
holders subsequently filed a motion for the appointment of an equity committee
with the U.S. Court.&#160; In December&nbsp;2009,
the U.S. Court entered an order denying the motion for an order appointing an
official committee of equity security holders.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Proposed Plan of Reorganization and Exit Credit Facilities</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In order
to successfully emerge from bankruptcy, the Company must propose and obtain
confirmation by the Bankruptcy Courts of a plan of reorganization that
satisfies the requirements of the Bankruptcy Code and the CCAA.&#160; A plan of reorganization would resolve the
Company&#146;s pre-petition obligations, set forth the revised capital structure of
the newly reorganized entity and provide for corporate governance subsequent to
the Company&#146;s exit from bankruptcy.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the
priority scheme established by the Bankruptcy Code and the CCAA, unless
creditors agree otherwise, pre-petition liabilities and post-petition
liabilities must be satisfied in full before SSCC&#146;s stockholders are entitled
to receive any distribution or retain any property under a plan of
reorganization.&#160; The ultimate recovery to
creditors and/or SSCC&#146;s stockholders, if any, will not be determined until
confirmation of a plan or plans of reorganization. No assurance can be given as
to what values, if any, will be ascribed to each of these constituencies or
what types or amounts of distributions, if any, they would receive. Because of
such possibilities, the value of the Company&#146;s liabilities and securities,
including SSCC&#146;s common stock, is highly speculative.&#160; Appropriate caution should be exercised with
respect to existing and future investments in any of the Company&#146;s liabilities
and/or securities.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">53<a name="PB_53_190207_7608"></a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">The
Proposed Plan of Reorganization</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;1,
2009, the Debtors filed their Joint Plan of Reorganization and Plan of
Compromise and Arrangement and Disclosure Statement with the U.S. Court.&#160; On December&nbsp;22, 2009, January&nbsp;27,
2010 and February&nbsp;4, 2010, the Debtors filed amendments to the Proposed
Plan of Reorganization (the &#147;Proposed Plan of Reorganization&#148;) and to the
Disclosure Statement (the &#147;Disclosure Statement&#148;).&#160; Key elements of the Proposed Plan of
Reorganization were as follows:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">the Company and SSCC would merge and become the reorganized
company (&#147;Reorganized Smurfit-Stone&#148;) that would be governed by a board of
directors that will include Patrick J. Moore, SSCC&#146;s current Chairman and Chief
Executive Officer, Steven J. Klinger, SSCC&#146;s current President and Chief
Operating Officer, and a number of independent directors, including a
non-executive chairman, to be selected by the Creditors&#146; Committee in
consultation with the Debtors;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">all of the existing secured debt of the Debtors would be
fully repaid with cash;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">substantially all of the existing unsecured debt and claims
against the Company, including all of the outstanding unsecured senior notes,
would be exchanged for common stock of the Reorganized Smurfit-Stone, which
would be traded on either the New York Stock Exchange or the NASDAQ market,
with holders of unsecured claims against the Company of less than or equal to
$10,000 entitled to receive payment of 100% of such claims in cash, and
eligible cash-out participants having the opportunity to indicate on their
ballot the percentage amount of their allowed claim they would be willing to
receive in cash in lieu of common stock;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">all of SSCC&#146;s existing equity securities would be cancelled
and existing shareholders of SSCC&#146;s common and Preferred Stock would receive no
distribution on account of their shares;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">the assets of the Canadian Debtors would be sold to a
newly-formed Canadian subsidiary of Reorganized Smurfit-Stone free and clear of
existing claims, liens and interests in exchange for (i)&nbsp;the repayment in
cash of the secured debt obligations of the Canadian Debtors, (ii)&nbsp;cash to
the Canadian Debtors&#146; unsecured creditors if they vote to accept the Proposed
Plan of Reorganization and (iii)&nbsp;the assumption of certain liabilities and
obligations of the Canadian Debtors; and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Reorganized Smurfit-Stone and its newly-formed Canadian
subsidiary would assume all of the existing obligations under the qualified
defined benefit pension plans in the United States and Canada sponsored by the
Debtors, as well as all of the collective bargaining agreements in the United
States and Canada between the Debtors and their labor unions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Proposed Plan of Reorganization will not become effective until certain
conditions are satisfied or waived, including: (i)&nbsp;entry of an order by
the Bankruptcy Courts confirming the Proposed Plan of Reorganization, (ii)&nbsp;all
actions, documents and agreements necessary to implement the Proposed Plan of
Reorganization having been effected or executed, (iii)&nbsp;access of the
Debtors to funding under the exit credit facility and (iv)&nbsp;specified
claims of the Debtors&#146; secured lenders having been paid in full pursuant to the
Proposed Plan of Reorganization.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;14,
2010, the U.S. Court granted approval to extend the Debtors&#146; exclusive right to
file a plan of reorganization to July&nbsp;21, 2010, and granted the Debtors
approval to solicit acceptance of a plan of reorganization until May&nbsp;21,
2011.&#160; If the Debtors&#146; exclusivity period
lapses, any party in interest would be able to file a plan of
reorganization.&#160; In addition to being
voted on by holders of impaired claims and equity interests, a plan of
reorganization must satisfy certain requirements of the Bankruptcy Code and the
CCAA and must be approved, or confirmed, by the Bankruptcy Courts in order to
become effective.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;29,
2010, the U.S. Court approved the Debtors&#146; Disclosure Statement as containing
adequate information for the holders of impaired claims and equity interest,
who are entitled to vote to accept or reject the Proposed Plan of
Reorganization.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Bankruptcy
Code requires the U.S. Court, after appropriate notice, to hold a hearing on
confirmation of a plan of reorganization.&#160;
The confirmation hearing on the Proposed Plan of Reorganization is
scheduled to begin on April&nbsp;14, 2010.&#160;
The confirmation hearing may be adjourned from time to time by the
Bankruptcy Court without further notice except for an announcement of the
adjourned date made at the confirmation hearing or any subsequent adjourned
confirmation hearing. There can be no assurance at this time that the Proposed
Plan of Reorganization will be confirmed by the Bankruptcy Courts or that any
such plan will be implemented successfully.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Exit
Credit Facilities</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;14,
2010, the U.S. Court entered an order authorizing the Debtors to (i)&nbsp;enter
into an exit term loan facility engagement and arrangement letter and fee
letters, (ii)&nbsp;pay associated fees and expenses and (iii)&nbsp;furnish
related indemnities.&#160;&#160; On February&nbsp;1,
2010, the Company filed a motion with the U.S. Court seeking approval to enter
into a senior secured term loan exit facility (the &#147;Term Loan Facility&#148;).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On February&nbsp;16,
2010, the U.S. Court granted the motion and authorized the Company and certain
of its affiliates to enter into the Term Loan Facility.&#160; On the same date, the U.S. Court also granted
the Company&#146;s February&nbsp;3, 2010 motion seeking approval to enter into a
commitment letter and fee letters for an asset-based revolving credit facility
(the &#147;ABL Revolving Facility&#148;) (together with the Term Loan Facility, the &#147;Exit
Credit Facilities&#148;).&#160; Based on such
approvals, on February&nbsp;22, 2010, the Company and certain of its
subsidiaries entered into the Term Loan Facility that provides for an aggregate
term loan commitment of $1,200 million.&#160;
In addition, the Company entered into a commitment letter and related
fee letters for the ABL Revolving Facility with aggregate commitments of $650
million (including a $100 million Canadian Tranche), which the Company expects
to enter into prior to exiting bankruptcy.&#160;&#160;
The ABL Revolving Facility will include a $150 million sub-limit for
letters of credit.&#160; The commitments for
the Term Loan Facility and the ABL Revolving Facility will terminate on July&nbsp;16,
2010 unless the Company&#146;s emergence from bankruptcy and satisfaction of certain
funding date conditions under the Term Loan Facility and the ABL Revolving
Facility occur on or prior to such date, and the Term Loan Facility is funded.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is permitted, subject
to obtaining lender commitments, to add one or more incremental facilities to
the Term Loan Facility in an aggregate amount up to $400 million.&#160; Each incremental facility is conditioned on (a)&nbsp;there
existing no defaults, (b)&nbsp;in the case of incremental term loans, such
loans have a final maturity no earlier than, and a weighted average life no
shorter than, the Term Loan Facility, and (c)&nbsp;after giving effect to one
or more incremental facilities, the consolidated senior secured leverage ratio
shall be less than 3.00 to 1.00.&#160; If the
interest rate spread applicable to any incremental facility exceeds the
interest rate spread applicable to the Term Loan Facility by more than 0.25%,
then the interest rate spread applicable to the Term Loan Facility will be
increased to equal the interest rate spread applicable to the incremental
facility.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On the
date the Company emerges from bankruptcy, the Term Loan will be funded and
borrowings are expected to be available under the ABL Revolving Facility.&#160;&#160; The proceeds of the borrowings under the
Term Loan Facility, together with available cash will be used to repay the
Company&#146;s outstanding secured indebtedness under its pre-petition Credit
Facility and pay fees, costs and expenses of approximately $50 million related
to and contemplated by the Exit Credit Facilities and the Proposed Plan of
Reorganization. Borrowings under the ABL Revolver Facility will be available
for working capital purposes, capital expenditures, permitted acquisitions and
general corporate purposes.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The term

Facility and is repayable in equal quarterly installments of $3 million

end of each fiscal year, varying percentages of the Company&#146;s excess cash flow,
as defined in the Term Loan Facility, based on certain agreed levels of secured
leverage ratios, must be used to repay outstanding&nbsp;principal amounts under
the Term Loan.&#160; Subject to specified
exceptions, the Term Loan Facility will also require the Company to use the net
</font></p>

plus the alternate base rate (the &#147;Term Loan ABR&#148;) defined as the greater of: (i)&nbsp;the
U.S. prime rate, (ii)&nbsp;the overnight federal funds rate plus 0.50%, or (iii)&nbsp;the
one month adjusted LIBOR rate plus 1.0%, provided that the Term Loan ABR shall
never be lower than 3.00% per annum, or (B)&nbsp;the adjusted LIBOR rate plus
4.75%, provided that the adjusted LIBOR rate shall never be lower than 2.00%

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

of the ABL Revolving Facility. The Company will have the option to borrow at a

US Prime Rate, (ii)&nbsp;the overnight federal funds rate plus 0.50% or (iii)&nbsp;LIBOR
rate plus 1.0%, or (B)&nbsp;the LIBOR rate plus 3.50% for the first 90 days
then 3.25% thereafter. The rate could be adjusted in the future from 3.25% to a
rate as high as 3.75% based on the average historical utilization under the ABL
Revolving Facility.&#160;&#160; The Company would
also pay either a 0.50% or 0.75% per annum unused commitment fee based on the
average historical utilization under the ABL Revolving Facility.&#160; The ABL Revolving Facility borrowings are
subject to a borrowing base derived from a formula based on certain eligible
accounts receivable and inventory, less certain reserves.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

under the Exit Credit Facilities will be guaranteed by Reorganized
Smurfit-Stone and certain of its subsidiaries, and would be secured by first
priority liens and second priority liens on substantially all its presently
owned and hereafter acquired assets and those of each of its subsidiaries party
to the Exit Credit Facilities, subject to certain exceptions and permitted
liens.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Exit
Credit Facilities contain affirmative and negative covenants that impose
restrictions on the Company&#146;s financial and business operations and those of
certain of its subsidiaries, including their ability to incur indebtedness,
incur liens, make investments, sell assets, pay dividends or make
acquisitions.&#160; The Exit Credit Facilities
contain events of default customary for financings of this type.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Going Concern Matters</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
consolidated financial statements and related notes have been prepared assuming
that the Company will continue as a going concern, although its bankruptcy
filings raise substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going
concern.&#160; The Company&#146;s ability to continue
as a going concern is dependent on restructuring its obligations in a manner
that allows it to obtain confirmation of a plan of reorganization by the
Bankruptcy Courts.&#160; The consolidated
financial statements do not include any adjustments related to the
recoverability and classification of recorded assets or to the amounts and
classification of liabilities or any other adjustments that might be necessary
should the Company be unable to continue as a going concern.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Financial
Reporting Considerations</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For periods
subsequent to the bankruptcy filings, the Company has applied the Financial
Accounting Standards Board (&#147;FASB&#148;) Accounting Standards Codification (&#147;ASC&#148;)
852, &#147;Reorganizations&#148; (&#147;ASC 852&#148;), in preparing the consolidated financial
statements.&#160; ASC 852 requires that the
financial statements distinguish transactions and events that are directly
associated with the reorganization from the ongoing operations of the
business.&#160; Accordingly, certain revenues,
expenses (including professional fees), realized gains and losses and
provisions for losses that are realized or incurred in the bankruptcy
proceedings have been recorded in reorganization items in the consolidated
statement of operations.&#160; In addition,
pre-petition obligations that may be impacted by the bankruptcy reorganization
process have been classified on the consolidated balance sheet in liabilities
subject to compromise .&#160; These
liabilities are reported at the amounts expected to be allowed by the Bankruptcy
Courts, even if they may be settled for lesser or greater amounts.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">amounts
expected to be allowed, even if they may be settled for lesser or greater
amounts.&#160; These liabilities represent the
amounts expected to be allowed on known or potential claims to be resolved
through the Chapter 11 and CCAA process, and remain subject to future
adjustments arising from negotiated settlements, actions of the Bankruptcy
Courts, rejection of executory contracts and unexpired leases, the
determination as to the value of collateral securing the claims, proofs of
claim, or other events.&#160; Liabilities
subject to compromise also include certain items, such as qualified defined
benefit pension and retiree medical obligations that may be assumed under the
Proposed Plan of Reorganization, and as such, may be subsequently reclassified
to liabilities not subject to compromise.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Bankruptcy Courts approved payment of certain pre-petition obligations,
including employee wages, salaries and benefits, and the payment of vendors and
other providers in the ordinary course for goods and services received after
the filing of the Chapter 11 Petition and the Canadian Petition and other
business-related payments necessary to maintain the operation of the Company&#146;s
business. Obligations associated with these matters are not classified as
liabilities subject to compromise.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has rejected certain
pre-petition executory contracts and unexpired leases with respect to the
Company&#146;s operations with the approval of the Bankruptcy Courts and may reject
additional contracts or unexpired leases in the future.&#160; Damages resulting from rejection of executory
contracts and unexpired leases are generally treated as general unsecured
claims and are classified as liabilities subject to compromise.</font></p>

<div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">2.&#160; Significant Accounting
Policies</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Basis of Presentation:</font></b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; The Company is a wholly owned subsidiary of
SSCC.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Nature of Operations:</font></b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; The Company&#146;s major operations are
containerboard, corrugated containers and reclamation.&#160; The Company&#146;s paperboard mills procure virgin
and reclaimed fiber and produce paperboard for conversion into corrugated
containers at Company-owned facilities and third-party converting operations.&#160; Paper product customers represent a diverse
range of industries including paperboard packaging and a broad range of
manufacturers of consumer goods.&#160;
Recycling operations collect or broker wastepaper for sale to
Company-owned and third-party paper mills.&#160;
Customers and operations are located principally in North America.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Principles of Consolidation:</font></b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; The consolidated financial statements include
the accounts of the Company and majority-owned and controlled
subsidiaries.&#160; Investments in
non-majority owned affiliates are accounted for using the equity method.&#160; Significant intercompany accounts and
transactions are eliminated in consolidation.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Cash and Cash Equivalents:</font></b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; The Company considers all highly liquid
investments with an original maturity of three months or less to be cash
equivalents.&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2009, the
Company had restricted cash of $9 million as approved by the U.S. Court to
provide financial assurance to certain utility vendors.&#160; Changes in restricted cash are reflected in
operating activities in the consolidated statements of cash flows.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Revenue Recognition:</font></b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; The Company recognizes revenue at the time
persuasive evidence of an agreement exists, price is fixed and determinable,
title passes to external customers and collectibility is reasonably
assured.&#160; Shipping and handling costs are
included in cost of goods sold.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company records certain inventory buy/sell transactions between counterparties
within the same line of business as a single exchange transaction on a net
basis in the consolidated statements of operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Receivables, Less Allowances:</font></b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; Credit is extended to customers based on an
evaluation of their financial condition.&#160;
The Company evaluates the collectibility of accounts receivable on a
case-by-case basis and makes adjustments to the bad debt reserve for expected
losses, considering such things as ability to pay, bankruptcy, credit ratings
and payment history.&#160; The Company also
estimates reserves for bad debts based on historical experience and past due
status of the accounts.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Inventories:</font></b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; Inventories are valued at the lower of cost
or market under the last-in, first-out (&#147;LIFO&#148;) method, except for $268 million
in 2009 and $296 million in 2008, which are valued at the lower of average cost
or market.&#160; First-in, first-out (&#147;FIFO&#148;)
costs (which approximate replacement costs) exceed the LIFO value by $94
million and $120 million at December&nbsp;31, 2009 and 2008, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Net Property, Plant and Equipment:</font></b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; Property, plant and
equipment are carried at cost.&#160; The costs
of additions, improvements and major replacements are capitalized, while
maintenance and repairs are charged to expense as incurred.&#160; Provisions for depreciation and amortization
are made using straight-line rates over the estimated useful lives of the related
assets and the shorter of useful lives or terms of the applicable leases for
leasehold improvements.&#160; Papermill
machines have been assigned a useful life of 18 to 23 years, while major
converting equipment has been assigned a useful life ranging from 12 to 20
years (See Note 7).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Timberland, Less Timber Depletion:</font></b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; Timberland is stated
at cost less accumulated cost of timber harvested.&#160; The portion of the costs of timberland
attributed to standing timber is charged against income as timber is cut, at
rates determined annually, based on the relationship of unamortized timber
costs to the estimated volume of recoverable timber.&#160; The costs of seedlings and reforestation of
timberland are capitalized.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">62<a name="PB_62_114731_7056"></a></font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Deferred Debt Issuance Costs and Losses From Extinguishment of Debt:</font></b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; Deferred debt
issuance costs are amortized over the terms of the respective debt obligations
using the interest method.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Long-Lived Assets:</font></b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; Long-lived assets held and used by the
Company are reviewed for impairment when events or changes in circumstances
indicate that their carrying amount may not be recoverable.&#160; Circumstances which could trigger a review
include, but are not limited to: significant decreases in the market price of
the asset; significant adverse changes in the business climate or legal
factors; accumulation of costs significantly in excess of the amount originally
expected for the acquisition or construction of the asset; current period cash
flow or operating losses combined with a history of losses or a forecast of
continuing losses associated with the use of the asset; and current expectation
that the asset will more likely than not be sold or disposed of significantly
before the end of its estimated useful life.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Recoverability
is assessed based on the carrying amount of the asset compared to the sum of
the undiscounted cash flows expected to result from the use and the eventual
disposal of the asset, as well as specific appraisal in certain instances.&#160; An impairment loss is recognized when the
carrying amount is not recoverable and exceeds fair value.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Once
the Company commits to a plan to abandon or take out of service a long-lived
asset before the end of its previously estimated useful life, depreciation
estimates are revised to reflect the use of the asset over its shortened useful
life (See Note 3).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Income Taxes:</font></b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; The Company accounts for income taxes in
accordance with the liability method of accounting for income taxes.&#160; Under the liability method, deferred assets
and liabilities are recognized based upon anticipated future tax consequences
attributable to differences between financial statement carrying amounts of
assets and liabilities and their respective tax bases.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company applies the provisions of ASC 740, &#147;Income Taxes&#148; (&#147;ASC 740&#148;), which
creates a single model to address accounting for uncertainty in tax positions
and clarifies the accounting for income taxes by prescribing a minimum
recognition threshold a tax position is required to meet before being
recognized in the financial statements.&#160;
Under the provisions of ASC 740, the Company elected to classify
interest and penalties related to unrecognized tax benefits in the Company&#146;s
income tax provision (See Note 14).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Foreign Currency:</font></b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; The functional currency for Canadian
operations is the U.S. dollar.&#160;
Fluctuations in Canadian dollar monetary assets and liabilities result
in gains or losses which are credited or charged to income.&#160; Foreign currency transactional gains or
losses are also credited or charged to income.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company&#146;s remaining foreign operations&#146; functional currency is the applicable
local currency.&#160; Assets and liabilities
for these foreign operations are translated at the exchange rate in effect at
the balance sheet date, and income and expenses are translated at average
exchange rates prevailing during the year.&#160;
Translation gains or losses are included within stockholders&#146; equity as
part of accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) (&#147;OCI&#148;) (See Note 17).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Derivatives and Hedging Activities:</font></b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; The Company&#146;s
derivative instruments were effectively terminated upon the filing of the
Chapter 11 Petition and the Canadian Petition.&#160;
Termination values were calculated based on potential settlement
value.&#160; Prior to the bankruptcy filing,
the Company recognized all derivatives on the balance sheet at fair value.&#160; Derivatives not qualifying for hedge
accounting were adjusted to fair value through income.&#160; Derivatives qualifying for cash flow hedge
accounting were recognized in OCI until the hedged item was recognized in
earnings.&#160; Hedges related to anticipated
transactions were designated and documented at hedge inception as cash flow
hedges and evaluated for hedge effectiveness quarterly (See Note 10).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Transfers of Financial Assets:</font></b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; Certain financial
assets were transferred to qualifying special-purpose entities and variable
interest entities where the Company is not the primary beneficiary.&#160; The assets and liabilities of such entities
are not reflected in the consolidated financial statements of the Company.&#160; Gains or losses on sale of financial assets
depend in part on the previous carrying amount of the financial </font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">63<a name="PB_63_114747_5335"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">assets
involved in the transfer, allocated between the assets sold and the retained
interests based on their relative fair value at the date of transfer.&#160; Quoted market prices are not available for
retained interests, so the Company estimates fair value based on the present
value of expected cash flows estimated by using management&#146;s best estimates of
key assumptions (See Note 8).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Stock-Based Compensation:&#160; </font></b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SSCC has stock-based employee compensation plans, including
stock options and restricted stock units (&#147;RSUs&#148;), which are recognized in the
financial statements based on the fair values as of the grant date.&#160; The stock options and RSUs are issued primarily
to certain employees of the Company (See Note 16).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Environmental Matters:</font></b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; The Company expenses environmental
expenditures related to existing conditions resulting from past or current
operations from which no current or future benefit is discernible.&#160; Expenditures that extend the life of the
related property or mitigate or prevent future environmental contamination are
capitalized.&#160; The Company records a
liability at the time when it is probable and can be reasonably estimated.&#160; Such liabilities are not discounted or
reduced for potential recoveries from insurance carriers.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Asset Retirement Obligations:</font></b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; The Company accounts for asset retirement
obligations in accordance with ASC 410, &#147;Accounting for Asset Retirement and
Environmental Obligations,&#148; which established accounting standards for the
recognition and measurement of an asset retirement obligation and its
associated asset retirement cost.&#160; It
also provides accounting guidance for legal obligations associated with the
retirement of tangible long-lived assets.&#160;
Asset retirement obligations recorded consist primarily of landfill
capping and closure and post-closure maintenance on the landfills.&#160; The Company has other asset retirement
obligations upon closure of facilities, principally costs for the closure of
wastewater treatment ponds and the removal of asbestos and chemicals, for which
retirement obligations are not recorded because the fair value of the liability
could not be reliably measured due to the uncertainty and timing of facility closures
or demolition.&#160; These asset retirement
obligations have indeterminate settlement dates because the period over which
the Company may settle these obligations is unknown and cannot be estimated.&#160; The Company will recognize a liability when
sufficient information is available to reasonably estimate its fair value (See
Note 13).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Restructuring:</font></b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; Costs associated with exit or disposal
activities are generally recognized when they are incurred rather than at the
date of a commitment to an exit or disposal plan (See Note 3).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Employee Benefit Plans:&#160; </font></b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the provisions of ASC 715, &#147;Compensation &#150; Retirement
Benefits&#148; (&#147;ASC 715&#148;), the funded status of the Company&#146;s defined benefit
pension plans and postretirement plans, measured as the difference between plan
assets at fair value and the benefit obligations, is recorded as an asset or
liability with the after-tax impact recorded to OCI based on an actuarial
valuation as of the balance sheet date.&#160;
Subsequent changes in the funded status of the plans are recognized in
OCI in the year in which the changes occur (See Note 15).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Use of Estimates:</font></b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; The preparation of financial statements in
conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (&#147;GAAP&#148;) requires
management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts
of assets and liabilities and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities
at the date of the financial statements and the reported amounts of revenues
and expenses during the reporting period.&#160;
Actual results could differ from those estimates.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Reclassifications:</font></b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; Certain reclassifications of prior year
presentations have been made to conform to the 2009 presentation.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Recently Adopted Accounting Standards:</font></b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; The FASB&#146;s Accounting Standards Codification 105
was released on July&nbsp;1, 2009 and became the single source of authoritative
U.S. GAAP.&#160; The change was established by
ASC 105, &#147;Generally Accepted Accounting Principles&#148; (&#147;ASC 105&#148;).&#160; Pursuant to the provisions of ASC 105, the
Company has updated its references to GAAP in its consolidated financial
statements issued for the period ended December&nbsp;31, 2009.&#160; The adoption of ASC 105 did not impact the
Company&#146;s financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">3.&#160; Restructuring Activities</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company continues to review and evaluate various restructuring and other
alternatives to streamline operations, improve efficiencies and reduce
costs.&#160; These actions subject the Company
to additional short-term costs, which may include facility shutdown costs,
asset impairment charges, lease commitment costs, severance costs and other closing
costs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
2009, the Company</font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">
</font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">closed 11 converting facilities
and permanently ceased production at the Ontonagon, Michigan medium mill and
the Missoula, Montana linerboard mill.&#160;
As a result of these closures and other ongoing initiatives, the Company
reduced its headcount by approximately 2,350 employees.&#160; The Company recorded restructuring charges of
$319 million, net of gains of $4 million from the sale of properties related to
previously closed facilities.&#160;
Restructuring charges included non-cash charges of $254 million related
to the write-down of assets, primarily property, plant and equipment, to
estimated net realizable values and the acceleration of depreciation for
converting equipment expected to be abandoned or taken out of service.&#160; The remaining charges of $69 million were
primarily for severance and benefits.&#160;
The net sales of the closed converting facilities in 2009 prior to
closure and for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2008 and 2007 were $62
million, $217 million and $258 million, respectively.&#160; The majority of these net sales are expected
to be transferred to other operating facilities.&#160; The Ontonagon, Michigan medium mill had
annual production capacity of 280,000 tons and the Missoula, Montana linerboard
mill had annual production capacity of 620,000 tons.&#160; Additional charges of up to $2 million are
expected to be recorded in future periods for severance and benefits related to
the closure of mill and converting facilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
2008, the Company</font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">
</font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">closed eight converting
facilities, announced the closure of two additional converting facilities and
permanently ceased operations of its containerboard machine at the Snowflake,
Arizona mill and production at the Pontiac pulp mill located in
Portage-du-Fort, Quebec.&#160; As a result of </font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

in 2007 prior to closure were $65 million.&#160;

idled machine at the Jacksonville, Florida mill with annual capacity to produce

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">4.&#160; Alternative Energy Tax Credits</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The U.S. Internal Revenue Code allowed an excise tax credit
for alternative fuel mixtures produced by a taxpayer for sale, or for use as a
fuel in a taxpayer&#146;s trade or business through December&nbsp;31, 2009, at which
time the credit expired.&#160; In May&nbsp;2009,
the Company was notified that its registration as an alternative fuel mixer was
approved by the Internal Revenue Service.&#160;
The Company, subsequently, submitted refund claims of approximately $654
million for the period December&nbsp;1, 2008 through December&nbsp;31, 2009
related to production at ten of its U.S. mills.&#160;
The Company received refund claims of approximately $595 million in </font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">67<a name="PB_67_115452_7748"></a></font></p>

the Company recorded other operating income of $633 million, net of fees and
expenses, in its consolidated statements of operations related to this matter.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">5.&#160; (Gain) Loss on Disposal of Assets</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;">In September&nbsp;2009, the Company completed the sale of
its Canadian timberlands for approximately $28 million, of which $1 million
remained in escrow at December&nbsp;31, 2009, pending completion of the title
registration process on certain parcels.&#160;
The proceeds from the sale were used to prepay a portion of the Canadian
DIP Term Loan (See Note 9).&#160; The Company
recorded a pretax loss of $2 million.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
September&nbsp;2007, the Company completed the sale of its Brewton, Alabama,
mill assets for $355 million. The Company received cash proceeds of $338
million, which excluded $16 million of accounts receivable previously sold to
Stone Receivables Corporation (&#147;SRC&#148;) under the accounts receivable
securitization program and was net of $1 million of other closing
adjustments.&#160; Substantially all of the
proceeds from the sale were applied directly to debt reduction.&#160; The Company recorded a pretax loss of $65
million, and a $32 million income tax provision, resulting in a net loss of $97
million.&#160; The after-tax loss was the
result of a provision for income taxes that was higher than the statutory
income tax rate due to non-deductible goodwill of $146 million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">6.&#160; Calpine Corrugated LLC</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the first quarter of 2008, the Company recorded a charge
of $22 million to fully reserve all amounts due from Calpine Corrugated LLC (&#147;Calpine
Corrugated&#148;).&#160; Calpine Corrugated,
formerly an independent corrugated container producer in Fresno, California for
which the Company was the primary containerboard supplier, experienced start-up
losses since it began operations in 2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On July&nbsp;29, 2008, the Company acquired a 90 percent
ownership interest in Calpine Corrugated.&#160;
In conjunction with the acquisition, the Company guaranteed
approximately $45 million of Calpine Corrugated&#146;s third party outstanding
debt.&#160; There was no cash consideration
paid.&#160; The transaction was accounted for
as a purchase business combination and the results of operations of Calpine
Corrugated are included in the consolidated statements of operations beginning July&nbsp;29,
2008.&#160; The purchase price allocation
completed in the fourth quarter of 2008 resulted in assets and liabilities of
approximately $50 million, including approximately $45 million of debt.&#160; No goodwill was recorded for the transaction.
&#160;The acquisition of Calpine Corrugated&#146;s
operations enabled the Company to accelerate the optimization of its Northern
California business unit and improve its position in the agricultural market
segment.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
2007, the Company recorded charges of $10 million to reserve for amounts due
from Calpine Corrugated.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Depreciation
expense was $364 million, $351 million and $355 million for 2009, 2008 and
2007, respectively.&#160; Property, plant and
equipment include capitalized leases of $19 million and $20 million and related
accumulated amortization of $17 million and $16 million at December&nbsp;31,
2009 and 2008, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">8.&#160; Transfers of Financial Assets</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;28, 2009, in conjunction with the filing of
the Chapter 11 Petition and the Canadian Petition, the accounts receivable
securitization programs were terminated and all outstanding receivables
previously sold to the non-consolidated financing entities were repurchased
with proceeds from borrowings under the DIP Credit Agreement (See Note 9).&#160; The repurchase of receivables of $385 million
has been included in the cash flows from financing activities in the
consolidated statement of cash flows.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Receivables Securitization Program</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Prior
to termination, the Company had a $450 million accounts receivable
securitization program whereby the Company sold, without recourse, on an
ongoing basis, certain of its accounts receivable to SRC, a wholly-owned
non-consolidated subsidiary of the Company.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SRC
transferred the receivables to a non-consolidated subsidiary, a limited
liability company which had issued notes to third-party investors.&#160; The Company had retained servicing
responsibilities and a subordinated interest in the limited liability
company.&#160; The Company received annual
servicing fees of 1% of the unpaid balance of the receivables and rights to
future cash flows arising after the investors in the securitization limited
liability company had received the return for which they had contracted.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SRC
was a qualified special&#150;purpose entity under the provisions of ASC 860, &#147;Transfers
and Servicing&#148; (&#147;ASC 860&#148;).&#160; Accordingly,
accounts receivable sold to SRC, for which the Company did not retain an
interest, were not included in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At
December&nbsp;31, 2008, $465 million of accounts receivable had been sold to
SRC, of which $97 million were retained by the Company as a subordinated
interest.&#160; The off-balance sheet SRC debt
at December&nbsp;31, 2008 was $365 million.&#160;
The Company&#146;s retained interest was carried at fair value and was
included in retained interest in receivables sold in the accompanying
consolidated balance sheet at December&nbsp;31, 2008.&#160; The Company recognized a loss on sales of
receivables to SRC of $14 million in 2008 which was included in other, net in
the consolidated statements of operations.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
