<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 52.55pt;text-indent:-52.55pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">ITEM 9.</font></b><b><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:8.5pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">CHANGES IN AND
DISAGREEMENTS WITH ACCOUNTANTS ON ACCOUNTING AND FINANCIAL DISCLOSURE</font></u></b><a name="Item9_ChangesInAndDisagreementsWi_164133"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 49.5pt;text-indent:-49.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">None.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-1.0in;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">ITEM 9A(T).</font></b><b><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:8.5pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">CONTROLS AND PROCEDURES</font></u></b><a name="Item9at_ControlsAndProcedures_164136"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls
and Procedures</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our management, with the
participation of our principal executive officer and our principal financial
officer, evaluated the effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures
(as defined in Exchange Act Rules&nbsp;13a-15(e)&nbsp;and 15d-15(e)) as of the
end of the period covered by this report and have concluded that, as of such
date, our disclosure controls and procedures were adequate and effective.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Changes in Internal Control</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There have not been any changes in
our internal control over financial reporting during the most recent quarter
that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect,
our internal control over financial reporting.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.75in;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">ITEM 9B.</font></b><b><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:8.5pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">OTHER INFORMATION</font></u></b><a name="Item9b_OtherInformation_164138"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pursuant to the authorization of the U.S. Court to continue
our performance-based short-term and long-term incentive plans, on
February&nbsp;24, 2010, our Compensation Committee adopted certain
modifications to the 2009 MIP for the 2010 MIP (each as defined below).&#160; Other than the modifications described in
this Item 9B. &#147;Other Information,&#148; all other terms and conditions of the 2009
MIP will continue with respect to the 2010 MIP.&#160;
The Committee reduced MIP performance targets for the NEOs for the
second six-month performance period under the 2010 MIP due, in part, to the
anticipated grants of equity described below upon our emergence from
bankruptcy.&#160; The MIP targets for the
second six-month performance period, expressed as a percentage of base salary,
for each of the NEOs will be as follows: 115% for Mr.&nbsp;Moore, 115% for
Mr.&nbsp;Klinger, 60% for Mr.&nbsp;Hunt, and 70% for Mr.&nbsp;Strickland. The
Committee did not approve an adjusted 2010 MIP target for Mr.&nbsp;Murphy
because he resigned from the Company effective as of February&nbsp;25, 2010,
but did approve a 70% post-emergence 2010 MIP target for any interim or new
Chief Financial Officer that may be appointed during 2010.&#160; In addition to the adjusted second six-month
performance period targets, the Committee also approved certain other modifications
to the 2010 MIP that will become effective after our emergence from bankruptcy
that will apply to the NEOs.&#160; These
additional modifications are: (1)&nbsp;the annual performance period will be
eliminated and each NEOs MIP bonus will be determined based upon our
performance for two six-month performance periods: (2)&nbsp;maximum Company
performance (140% of the performance target) will earn a 200% payout of the
NEOs target MIP bonus; and (3)&nbsp;earned MIP bonuses will be paid annually.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Also on February&nbsp;24, 2010, the Committee approved,
subject to confirmation of our Proposed Plan of Reorganization, equity grants
to certain of the currently employed NEOs upon emergence from bankruptcy,
including an award of 0.900% of our New Common Stock for Mr.&nbsp;Klinger, and
0.153% of our New Common Stock for each of Messrs.&nbsp;Hunt and
Strickland.&#160; Approximately 76% of each
NEOs equity grant will be made in the form of a stock option award, and
approximately 24% in the form of restricted shares.&#160; Mr.&nbsp;Moore will not receive an equity
grant upon emergence from bankruptcy due to his anticipated retirement, and
Mr.&nbsp;Murphy will not receive an equity grant because of his resignation.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Committee elected not to evaluate base salaries for the
NEOs until after our emergence from bankruptcy, with the exception of
Mr.&nbsp;Strickland&#146;s base salary, which the Committee increased to $415,000
effective March&nbsp;1, 2010 due to his assumption of additional
responsibilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Committee also approved two
forms of amended and restated employment security agreements for Mr.&nbsp;Hunt
and Mr.&nbsp;Strickland and certain of our other Senior Vice Presidents other
than the NEOs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">PART&nbsp;III<a name="Partiii_164140"></a></font></b></h2>

<h2 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.75in;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">ITEM 10.</font></b><b><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:8.5pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">DIRECTORS, EXECUTIVE OFFICERS AND CORPORATE GOVERNANCE</font></u></b><a name="Item10_DirectorsExecutiveOfficers_164141"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 45.0pt;text-indent:-45.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h1 align="left" style="font-weight:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:left;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Directors</font></u></b></h1>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Set forth below is certain
information concerning our board of directors (Board of Directors).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Steven J. Klinger, </font></b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">born March&nbsp;5,
1959, was appointed President and Chief Operating Officer on May&nbsp;11, 2006.
Prior to joining SSCE, Mr.&nbsp;Klinger was employed by Georgia Pacific

Ownership Reporting Compliance</font></u></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Section&nbsp;16(a)&nbsp;of the
Securities Exchange Act of 1934 requires the Executive Officers and Directors,
and persons who beneficially own more than ten percent of the Common Stock, to
file initial reports of ownership and reports of changes in ownership with the
SEC. Executive Officers, Directors and greater than ten percent beneficial
owners are required by SEC regulations to furnish the Company with copies of
all Section&nbsp;16(a)&nbsp;forms they file. Based solely on a review of the
copies of such forms furnished to the Company and written representations from
the Executive Officers and Directors, the Company believes that during the
period from January&nbsp;1, 2009 through December&nbsp;31, 2009, its Executive
Officers, Directors and greater than ten percent beneficial owners complied
with all Section&nbsp;16(a)&nbsp;filing requirements applicable to them.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">COMPENSATION DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS</font></b></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Introduction</font></b></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As used in this
Item 11, the terms &#147;SSCC&#148; and the &#147;Company&#148; are used interchangeably since
compensation of the Executive Officers of the Company is determined by the SSCC&#146;s
Compensation Committee (the Committee), and the Executive Officers are not
separately compensated for their services as Executive Officers of SSCC and the
Company.&#160; SSCC is a holding company with
no business </font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">97<a name="PB_97_164302_5335"></a></font></p>

<div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">operations of its
own, and there is no intercompany allocation with regard to any services provided
by the Executive Officers to SSCC.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The purpose of this
discussion is to describe the compensation philosophy of SSCC and how this
philosophy is applied to the compensation of the named executive officers
(NEOs).&#160;&#160; As noted herein the
Compensation Committee (the Committee) has responsibility for evaluating and
determining the compensation of executive officers.&#160; The overall goal of the Committee is to
assure that compensation paid to the NEOs is fair, reasonable and competitive,
and is linked to increasing the long-term enterprise value of SSCC.&#160; The executives that this discussion covers
are:</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Patrick J.
Moore, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Steven J.
Klinger, President and Chief Operating Officer</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">John R.
Murphy, Former Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer*</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Craig A.

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Philosophy
and Objectives of Compensation Programs</font></b></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In accordance with
the overall goal of the Committee described above, the Company&#146;s compensation
programs have followed the objectives listed below:</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Compensation
should be competitive with the market.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Compensation
should be significantly performance-based.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Compensation
should have a significant long-term component.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">To balance these
objectives, our executive compensation program uses the following elements:</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Base
salary: to provide a minimum level of market competitiveness.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Short-term
incentives: to recognize short-term operating performance.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Long-term
incentives:&#160; to align executives with the
long-term value creation of the enterprise.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The significant
impact of the economic downturn on the Company and the Company&#146;s bankruptcy
filing in January&nbsp;2009 made it inappropriate to continue the equity-based
component of the annual and long-term incentive awards.&#160; We will describe below how our 2009 and 2010 programs
continued to meet these overall objectives, despite this constraint.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Compensation
Committee Practices</font></b></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Committee
typically holds at least one meeting each year to review information prepared
by its consultant and management relevant to the establishment of the elements
of compensation for executive officers for the following year. The Committee
then holds meetings to review all of the elements of compensation of the
executive officers, individually and in comparison to each other, as well as
benefits and perquisites, benefits accrued under retirement plans, and
compensation and benefits payable following the termination of employment under
employment and severance agreements. The Committee then approves changes in all
elements of compensation for the executive officers at one time. The Committee
held six meetings in 2009 and has held two meetings in 2010. Due to the nature
of the bankruptcy proceedings the Committee met more frequently than normal in
2009.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Use of Consultants and
Benchmarking</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Committee has the authority to
retain, terminate and compensate consultants to provide information and counsel
to the Committee. The Committee has engaged Hewitt Associates,&nbsp;LLC
(Hewitt) to provide executive and director compensation consulting services
since 2003. Hewitt provides the Committee with research and analysis on
competitive data and guidance on overall compensation trends and strategies.
Hewitt collects and analyzes executive compensation data from two comparator
groups: a peer group of nine companies that the Committee believes are the most
relevant direct competitors of the Company, which have median annual sales of
$4.0&nbsp;billion (Boise Cascade&nbsp;LLC, Graphic Packaging Corporation,
International Paper Company, MeadWestvaco Corporation, Packaging Corporation of
America, Pactiv Corporation, Sonoco Products Company, Temple Inland&nbsp;Inc.,
and Weyerhaeuser Company) (the Peer Group), and a broader group of 83
industrial companies of similar size and complexity to the Company, which have
median annual sales of approximately $7.6&nbsp;billion (the General Group).
Hewitt annually conducts this analysis for the Committee in the categories of
base salaries, annual incentive targets and awards, long-term incentives, total
compensation, and target total compensation, and measures the compensation of
each of the executive officers against the median of their counterparts of the
Peer Group and the General Group. The Committee uses this analysis as the basis
for comparing the Company&#146;s compensation against general market trends in light
of the performance of the Company, the paper packaging industry, and industrial
companies in general. Hewitt does not make specific recommendations as to the
level of any element of compensation of any Executive Officer.&#160; Hewitt also supported the Committee in
determining the appropriateness of its programs in the bankruptcy context.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Role of Management</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Committee seeks the
recommendation of the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer as to adjustments in
the amount of base salary and the amount of long-term incentive awards for each
of the other executive officers. The Committee also seeks the recommendation of
the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer and the Senior Vice President&#151;Human
Resources as to the annual target levels and the design and weighting of
performance objectives for the annual incentives of the executive officers
(other than the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer). The Committee
periodically approves levels of long-term incentive awards and authorizes the
Senior Vice President&#151;Human Resources to grant such awards to non-executive
officers, including non-executive officers hired between the dates of meetings
of the Committee or the Board to the extent necessary to induce such employees
to join the Company.&#160;&#160; For 2009, the
Committee approved the design and the targets for both the short-term and
long-term incentive programs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Elements of Compensation and 2009
and 2010 Compensation Decisions</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">General</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Committee has designed each
element of compensation for executive officers to further the philosophy and
objectives set forth above and to support and enhance the business strategy of
the Company.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Base Salaries</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">It is the intent of the Committee to
maintain base salary levels of executive officers at or near the median levels
of comparable companies (using the data for the two comparator groups provided
by Hewitt). The Committee makes adjustments in base salary once per year, to be
effective on April&nbsp;1, except in case of promotions or other exceptional
circumstances that justify adjustments outside of the annual review process.
Adjustments in base salary are based on the performance of the Executive
Officer and the relationship of his or her salary to the median of the
comparator groups; however, it has been the practice of the Committee to make
gradual adjustments in base salaries over a multi-year period to address
market-based differences, rather than large one-year adjustments. In light of
the bankruptcy proceedings and the current economic environment, the Chairman
and Chief Executive Officer did not recommend any base salary increases for
NEOs in 2009, and the Committee approved no salary increases for NEOs in 2009
(including the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer).&#160;&#160; In light of our anticipated emergence from
bankruptcy proceedings in the second quarter of 2010, it is not anticipated
that base salaries for the NEOs for 2010 will be evaluated until after
emergence, with the exception of Mr. Strickland&#146;s base salary, which will
increase to $415,000 effective March 1, 2010 due to his assumption of
additional responsibilities.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Short-term Incentives</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Management Incentive Plan (MIP)
is generally designed to incentivize management to drive short-term operating
results. On April&nbsp;22, 2009, the U.S. Court authorized the Company to
continue its performance-based short-term incentives for 2009 pursuant to the
terms and conditions contained in the U.S. Court&#146;s order (the Order).&#160; For 2009, annual and semi-annual incentives
were paid pursuant to the 2009 Management Incentive Plan (the 2009 MIP).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Because of the
significant uncertainty around the Company&#146;s business and the economy, the
Committee felt it appropriate to make certain modifications to the MIP for
2009. The 2009 MIP encompassed three performance periods, with the following
payout weights:</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

through June&nbsp;30, 2009&#160; was set at
40% of individual target.</font></p>

Committee reviewed the individual targets for market appropriateness and
internal equity.&#160; This analysis resulted
in adjustments for the NEOs. The aggregate 2009 MIP targets, expressed as a
percentage of base salary, for each of the NEOs were as follows: 125% for Mr.&nbsp;Moore,
125% for Mr.&nbsp;Klinger, 100% for Mr.&nbsp;Murphy, 80% for Mr.&nbsp;Hinrichs,
100% for Mr.&nbsp;Hunt, and 100% for Mr.&nbsp;Strickland.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Prior to 2008 a
portion of the earned MIP award was paid in restricted shares.&#160; Due to the inappropriateness of using equity
as a payout vehicle during the bankruptcy process, the Committee (consistent
with the Order) designed the 2009 MIP payments to be paid entirely in cash.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Based upon the
approved 2009 MIP, the first semi-annual payment (40% of target) was paid based
upon performance for the first semi-annual performance period (January&nbsp;1</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">st</font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;to June&nbsp;30</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">th</font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">).&#160;&#160; Performance for the first semi-annual
performance period exceeded the maximum DCA Adjusted EBITDAR performance
relative to budget, resulting in a 175% payout.&#160;
Per the terms of the 2009 MIP, executives were paid at target (100%).&#160; The remaining 75% payment for the first
semi-annual performance period was paid after </font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">* Mr.&nbsp;Murphy
joined us on May&nbsp;18, 2009, and was not eligible to participate in the 2009
MIP for the first semi-annual performance period.&#160; Mr.&nbsp;Hinrichs employment with us
terminated on May&nbsp;18, 2009 and he received a prorated MIP payment for the
first semi-annual performance period.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Order also provided for the continuation
of the MIP into 2010, if the bankruptcy case was not resolved by the beginning
of the plan year.&#160; For 2010, this plan
would replicate the 2009 MIP (performance periods and payout curve).&#160; The specific DCA Adjusted EBITDAR targets and
individual targets for the performance periods for 2010 were adjusted to
reflect the business conditions for 2010 and were developed in consultation
with the Creditors&#146; Committee and reviewed by other stakeholders, as defined in
the Order.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Committee reviewed certain
aspects of the 2010 MIP for continued market appropriateness and internal
equity in the anticipated event that we emerge from bankruptcy in 2010.&#160; This analysis resulted in anticipated
reductions of the 2010 MIP targets for the NEOs for the second six-month
performance period under the 2010 MIP due, in part, to the anticipated grants
of equity to the NEOs that are described below and are subject to confirmation
of our Proposed Plan of Reorganization.&#160;
The MIP targets for the second six-month performance period, expressed
as a percentage of base salary, for each of the NEOs will be as follows: 115%
for Mr. Moore, 115% for Mr. Klinger, 60% for Mr. Hunt, and 70% for Mr.
Strickland.&#160; The Committee did not
approve an adjusted 2010 MIP target for Mr. Murphy because he resigned from his
employment with us effective as of February 25, 2010, but did approve a 70%
post-emergence 2010 MIP target for any interim or new Chief Financial Officer
that may be appointed during 2010.&#160; In
addition to the post-emergence 2010 MIP targets, the Committee also approved
certain modifications to the 2010 MIP that will become effective after we
emergence from bankruptcy that will apply to the NEOs:&#160; (1) the annual performance period will be eliminated
and each NEOs MIP bonus will be determined based upon our performance for two
six-month performance periods: (2) maximum Company performance (140% of the
performance target) will earn a 200% payout of the NEOs target MIP bonus; and
(3) earned MIP bonuses will be paid annually.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Long-Term Incentives</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As stated above, granting equity to
executives during the bankruptcy proceedings is not appropriate. The Committee
oversaw a redesign of the our long-term incentives that were historically a mix
of stock options and restricted stock (pursuant to the 2004 Long-Term Incentive
Plan) into a performance-based cash plan, the 2009 Long-Term Incentive Plan
(2009 LTIP).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">2009 LTIP</font></u><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">. The 2009
LTIP was approved by the Committee and the U.S. Court (in the Order described
above).&#160; Each participant is eligible to
receive a potential payout subject to performance achieved in a two-year
performance cycle that began on January&nbsp;1, 2009 and runs through the
earlier of emergence from bankruptcy or December&nbsp;31, 2010.&#160; This plan is designed to incentivize
management to achieve a combination of operating performance and restructuring
goals which the Committee believes supports the goal of increasing the
enterprise value of SSCC.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Specifically,
the 2009 LTIP has two metrics.&#160; Each
metric is weighted 50% for payout purposes.&#160;
Each metric will be assessed independently on the specific performance
criteria.&#160; The first metric is a
financial performance metric based upon the achievement of DCA Adjusted EBITDAR
for the full calendar years of 2009 and 2010 (pro-rated as appropriate for 2010
if we emerge from our bankruptcy proceedings in 2010).&#160; The second metric is a restructuring goal
based upon the average trading price of our publicly traded bonds during the
thirty days preceding our emergence from the bankruptcy proceedings.&#160; Additional information concerning these
performance metrics is set forth in our Proposed Plan of Reorganization filed
in our bankruptcy proceedings.</font></p>

grant upon emergence from bankruptcy because he resigned from his employment
with us prior to our emergence from bankruptcy.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Other Benefits and Perquisites</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We provide customary benefits to
executive officers such as group insurance and company-sponsored savings plans
that are generally available to all other salaried employees. We provide
perquisites to executive officers not available to salaried employees
generally, which in most cases are limited to an additional level of group term
life insurance for Mr.&nbsp;Moore, and executive physicals, supplemental
disability benefits and reimbursement for financial, tax planning and certain
legal services for Messrs.&nbsp;Moore and Klinger. The perquisites provided to
NEOs are limited by the terms of their employment agreements and are more fully
described in footnote (f)&nbsp;to the Summary Compensation Table under &#147;Executive
Compensation&#148;.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Committee had also established a
policy as described below to allow the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer to
use the Company aircraft for personal use for up to 30&nbsp;hours per year and
to receive a gross-up payment in connection with the taxable income attributed
to him as the result of receiving this benefit. This policy was intended to
accommodate personal travel that may be adjunct to business travel, in which
the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer utilizes the Company aircraft for
security and convenience. This policy was eliminated in 2009 when we elected
not to retain our Company aircraft.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Post-Termination Benefits</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">All of the executive officers hired
by us prior to January&nbsp;1, 2006 participate in our qualified pension plan
for salaried employees. Depending on the date of hire and legacy company,
different executive officers participate in different supplemental
non-qualified pension plans for salaried employees. Mr.&nbsp;Moore participates
in the Jefferson Smurfit Corporation Supplemental Income Pension Plan II.&#160; Mr.&nbsp;Hunt participates in the Jefferson
Smurfit Corporation Supplemental Income Pension Plan III.&#160; Messrs.&nbsp;Murphy and Strickland are not
eligible to participate in any pension plan.&#160;
We entered into an Executive Retirement Agreement with Mr.&nbsp;Klinger
at the time of his employment in 2006 that provides substantial non-qualified
pension benefits equivalent to what he had in place with his prior employer,
offset by the benefits actually received from his prior employer<i>.&#160; </i>In 2007, we announced our intent to freeze
our salaried pension plan effective December&nbsp;31, 2008 to address the
ongoing cost of the pension plan to us, and implemented an enhanced salaried
401(k)&nbsp;savings plan benefit as of January&nbsp;1, 2009.<i>  </i>&#160;See &#147;Pension Plans&#148; for a more complete
description of each plan.&#160; It is anticipated
that all of the non-qualified post-termination benefits will be considered
pre-petition unsecured claims in our bankruptcy proceedings, except as set
forth in the </font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

with Mr.&nbsp;Moore and Mr.&nbsp;Klinger that are anticipated to become
effective upon emergence from bankruptcy proceedings that provide for the
assumption of such benefits.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Employment and Severance
Agreements</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Prior to commencement of bankruptcy
proceedings, the Board approved Employment Agreements for Mr.&nbsp;Moore, Mr.&nbsp;Klinger
and Mr.&nbsp;Hinrichs. See &#147;Employment Agreements and Post-Termination Payments&#148;.&#160; The agreement with Mr.&nbsp;Hinrichs was
terminated in connection with his resignation from the Company.&#160;&#160; In anticipation of emergence from
bankruptcy, the Committee approved amended and restated Employment Agreements
for Mr.&nbsp;Moore and Mr.&nbsp;Klinger, which will become effective upon our
emergence from bankruptcy.&#160; The Committee
and the Board believe that retention of these two executive officers is
critical to the our success as we transition from bankruptcy, and that these
Employment Agreements are beneficial to us by providing strong incentives on
the part of these executive officers to remain employed with us for the periods
specified in the individual arrangements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Additionally, prior to the
bankruptcy filing, the Board or the Committee also had approved Employment
Security Agreements for each of our other Senior Vice Presidents, which provide
for payments under certain circumstances following a change of control of the
Company. See &#147;Employment Agreements and Post-Termination Payments&#148;.&#160; It is anticipated that these agreements will
not be assumed by us in the bankruptcy proceedings.&#160;&#160;&#160; Certain of these executives will be parties
to one of the forms of amended and restated employment security agreements
approved by the Committee to be effective upon our emergence from bankruptcy. The
Committee believes that these agreements are beneficial to us by providing for
the retention and continuity of service of these executive officers who will
continue to be critical to our success after we emerge from our bankruptcy
proceedings.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Policies Related to Compensation</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition to the actions taken by
the Committee in accordance with the philosophy and objectives described above,
we have in place some specific policies relating to compensation matters that
have been adopted as warranted in order to institute and document controls over
certain aspects of the compensation process. Policies that impact the
compensation of executive officers are adopted and amended by the Board or the
Committee, and policies applicable to all salaried employees generally are
adopted and amended by management, at the direction of either the Chairman and
Chief Executive Officer or the Senior Vice President&#151;Human Resources. Policies
that impact our retirement and savings plans are approved by the Administrative
Committee of such plans, which is comprised of members of management.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Compensation-related
policies approved by the Board or the Committee (some of which have been
suspended due to our bankruptcy proceedings) include:</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#149; <i>Executive Stock Ownership Guidelines.</i>&nbsp;&nbsp;Each
Executive Officer is required to own Common Stock with a value equal to a
multiple of his or her base salary at the time of appointment or promotion into
such a position. The multiple for the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer is
three times base salary; the multiple for the President and Chief Operating
Officer and the Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer is two times
base salary; and the multiple for all other executive officers is one time base
salary. Compliance was required by the later of December&nbsp;31, 2007 or
within three years of the date of promotion or appointment. This policy has
been suspended indefinitely due to the bankruptcy proceedings.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#149; <i>Limitation on Severance Payments.</i>&nbsp;&nbsp;Unless
approved or ratified by the holders of a majority of our outstanding Common
Stock, the Committee will not approve any agreements with any Executive Officer
that provide for the payment upon retirement or other termination of employment
of benefits (other than those payable in the ordinary course pursuant to
retirement plans) in excess of 2.99 times the aggregate amount of the Executive
Officer&#146;s then-current salary, bonus and perquisites.&#160; We have suspended this policy based upon our
current circumstances, and expect to revisit this policy upon emergence from
bankruptcy.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#149; <i>Equity Award Practices.</i>&nbsp;&nbsp;In December&nbsp;2006,
the Committee adopted a set of practices that prescribe that a grant of stock
options may only be approved at meetings of the Board or the Committee, and not
by written consent in lieu of a meeting; that the grant date for options
granted </font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">103<a name="PB_103_165628_7608"></a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">by the
Senior Vice President&#151;Human Resources pursuant to authority delegated to him by
the Committee relating to non-executive officers shall be the fifth business
day of the calendar month immediately following the first day worked, for any
newly-hired employee, or the effective date of any promotion or other change in
employment circumstance for any current employee; and that no discretionary
awards of stock options can be made to any Executive Officer. We do not grant
stock options based on the timing of the announcement of material non-public
information and prohibit the backdating or repricing of stock options. The
Committee does not expect to grant any additional stock options during the
pendency of the bankruptcy proceedings.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Tax and Accounting Implications</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Committee reviews and considers
the deductibility of executive compensation under Section&nbsp;162(m)&nbsp;of
the Internal Revenue Code, which provides that we may not deduct compensation
of more than $1&nbsp;million to certain persons. We believe that payments under
the 2009 MIP are fully tax-deductible. The Committee considers accounting
treatment in the process of making decisions regarding executive compensation,
but makes executive compensation decisions based on the philosophy and
objectives set forth above, and not primarily on the basis of tax or accounting
treatment.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Conclusion</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Committee believes that the
total compensation of each of the executive officers, including the NEOs
discussed in the tabular presentations in this annual report on Form&nbsp;10-K,
is reasonable and not excessive, and is in line with our Compensation
Philosophy.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">COMPENSATION COMMITTEE INTERLOCKS
AND INSIDER PARTICIPATION</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">No member of the Committee currently
is or was during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009, an officer, former
officer or employee of ours or any of our subsidiaries. During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2009, no Executive Officer of ours served as a member of (i)&nbsp;the
compensation committee of another entity in which one of the executive officers
of such entity served on the Committee, (ii)&nbsp;the board of directors of
another entity in which one of the executive officers of such entity served on
the Committee, or (iii)&nbsp;the compensation committee of another entity in
which one of the executive officers of such entity served as a member of the
Board.&#160; During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2009, no member of the Committee had any relationship requiring disclosure by
us under any paragraph of Item 404 of Regulation S-K.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">COMPENSATION COMMITTEE REPORT</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Committee has reviewed and
discussed the Compensation Discussion and Analysis with management and, based
on such review and discussions, the Committee recommended to our Board that the
Compensation Discussion and Analysis be included in our Annual Report on Form&nbsp;10-K
for the fiscal year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009.</font></p>

earned by each of our&#160; NEOs, for the
fiscal year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009. The three primary elements of
compensation (base salary, short-term incentives and long-term incentives), as
well as other benefits and perquisites, are discussed in detail under &#147;Compensation
Discussion and Analysis.&#148; Pension benefits payable to the NEOs are discussed in
detail under &#147;Pension Plans,&#148; and detailed information regarding compensation

the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 were $2,079,104 for Mr.&nbsp;Moore;
$1,493,123 for Mr.&nbsp;Klinger; $240,685 for Mr.&nbsp;Murphy; $89,173 for Mr.&nbsp;Hinrichs;

were paid entirely in cash for 2009, were paid in two installments on July&nbsp;31,
2009 and January&nbsp;29, 2010 (except for Mr.&nbsp;Hinrichs, who was paid in
one installment on July&nbsp;31, 2009), and are disclosed in the Non-Equity

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .3in;text-indent:-.3in;"><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:8.0pt;">(a)</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:8.0pt;">Amounts shown under &#147;BONUS&#148; for Mr.&nbsp;
Hunt and Mr.&nbsp;Strickland in 2008 represent cash bonuses paid in connection
with significant corporate transactions, and for Mr.&nbsp;Strickland in 2009 a
payment in lieu of club initiation fees pursuant to our commitment in
connection with his joining us.&#160; The
amount shown under this column for Mr.&nbsp;Murphy in 2009 represents a
discretionary payment to Mr.&nbsp;Murphy in recognition of his service with us
from May&nbsp;18, 2009, when he joined us, to June&nbsp;30, 2009.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .3in;text-indent:-.3in;"><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:8.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .3in;text-indent:-.3in;"><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:8.0pt;">(b)</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:8.0pt;">Amounts shown under &#147;STOCK AWARDS&#148;
reflect the grant date fair value, computed in accordance with FASB&#146;s
Accounting Standards Codification Topic 718 (formerly SFAS&nbsp;123(R)), of
RSUs awarded to the NEOs under the LTIP in 2007 and 2008.&#160; In addition, the NEOs were required to defer
50% of their MIP award into RSUs for the 2007 MIP, and we matched 20% of the
amount deferred in the form of RSUs, which vest after three years.&#160; The deferred amount and Company match are
included in the amounts shown in the column titled &#147;STOCK AWARDS&#148; for 2007.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .3in;text-indent:-.3in;"><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:8.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .3in;text-indent:-19.6pt;"><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:8.0pt;">(c)</font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="1" face="Arial" style="font-size:8.0pt;">Amounts shown under &#147;OPTION AWARDS&#148;

this column under &#147;TARGET&#148; reflect the NEOs&#146; award under the MIP for 2009,
which may be more or less than the target MIP award established for the
respective NEO under the 2009 MIP.&#160;
Amounts shown in this column under &#147;THRESHOLD&#148; and &#147;MAXIMUM&#148; reflect the
minimum and maximum award the NEO could have received under the MIP for 2009.
Meeting the threshold performance level for MIP awards entitles the NEOs to the
minimum award (50% of the target MIP award), and MIP awards are capped at 1.75
times the target MIP award for each of the NEOs for 2009 (125% of salary for Messrs.&nbsp;Moore
and Klinger, 100% of salary for Messrs.&nbsp;Murphy, Hunt and Strickland and
80% of salary for Mr.&nbsp;Hinrichs).</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We provide
retirement benefits to each of the NEOs (other than Messrs.&nbsp;Klinger,
Murphy and Strickland) under a tax-qualified defined benefit pension plan (the
Smurfit-Stone Container Corporation Pension Plan for Salaried Employees (the
Pension Plan, or the JSC Pension Plan or Universal Pension Plan, as defined
below)) and one of three non-qualified defined benefit pension plans (the
Jefferson Smurfit Corporation Supplemental Income Pension Plan II (SIPP II),
the Jefferson Smurfit Corporation Supplemental Income Pension Plan III/Stone
Top-Hat Plan/St.&nbsp;Laurent Paperboard Executive Supplemental Retirement Plan
(SIPP&nbsp;III), or the plan established pursuant to the Executive Retirement
Agreement with Mr.&nbsp;Klinger (the Klinger Retirement Agreement)). Benefits
provided under the Pension Plan are based on one of two sets of plan provisions
for service prior to January&nbsp;1, 2007. Benefits for employees of the former
Jefferson Smurfit Corporation are determined under the Jefferson Smurfit
Corporation Pension Plan (the JSC Pension Plan).&#160; For service after December&nbsp;31, 2006,
benefits are based on the provisions of the Universal Pension Plan. All benefit
accruals in the Pension Plan ceased as of December&nbsp;31, 2008. The following
table discloses information regarding the present value of the current accrued
pension benefits of the NEOs computed as of December&nbsp;31, 2009. There were
no payments made to the NEOs pursuant to these plans during the last fiscal
year. See &#147;Compensation Discussion and Analysis&#151;Post-Termination Benefits&#148; for
additional information regarding our pension plans.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">PENSION PLANS</font></b></p>

<p align="left" style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Subject to
final approval of our Proposed Plan of Reorganization, it is anticipated that
the qualified pension plans described
below will be assumed by the Reorganized Smurfit-Stone.&#160; The non-qualified plans will not be assumed,
and claims for benefits under these plans will be unsecured claims in the
bankruptcy proceedings, with the exception of the claims of Messrs.&nbsp;Moore
and Klinger, that will be waived in connection with the execution of their
respective New Agreements (as defined below in the section titled &#147;Employment
Agreements and Post-Termination Payments&#148;) in exchange for certain retirement
benefits provided to them in those New Agreements.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Tax-Qualified Pension Plan</font></b></p>

<p align="left" style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Salaried
employees hired before January&nbsp;1, 2006 are eligible to participate in this
plan. The plan provisions that apply for benefit accruals before January&nbsp;1,
2007 are based on the company with which the employee originally became
employed. For accruals after December&nbsp;31, 2006, the Universal Pension Plan
provisions apply. All benefit accruals ceased as of December&nbsp;31, 2008. The
normal form of payment is a single life annuity with survivor options provided
on an actuarially equivalent basis.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Jefferson Smurfit Corporation Pension Plan</font></b></p>

<p align="left" style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Participants
earn service for the period of employment prior to January&nbsp;1, 2007. The
benefit formula is 1.5% of final average earnings minus 1.2% of the primary
insurance amount, all multiplied by years of service. Earnings include total
compensation except for payments under annual incentive plans, and any
long-term incentive program or employment contract, up to the applicable
tax-qualified plan compensation limit ($230,000 in 2008). Final average
earnings are the average of the highest five consecutive years of earnings out
of the last 10&nbsp;years prior to December&nbsp;31, 2008. Participants vest in
their benefits after completing five years of service with us. The normal
retirement age is age 65, but participants who complete 25&nbsp;years of
service or are age 55 with five years of service may elect to retire early.
Benefits are reduced by 5% per year from age 65 if the participant has less
than 10&nbsp;years of service at termination and from age 62 if the participant
has at least 10&nbsp;years of service.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Universal Pension Plan</font></b></p>

<p align="left" style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Participants
earn service for the period of employment with us for the period after December&nbsp;31,
2006 and prior to January&nbsp;1, 2009. The benefit formula is 0.9% of final
average earnings plus 0.4% of final average earnings in excess of covered
compensation, all multiplied by years of service up to 30&nbsp;years (or
30&nbsp;years less service earned prior to January&nbsp;1, 2007 under the
predecessor plan). Earnings include total compensation except for payments
under the MIP, certain other annual incentive plans and any long-term incentive
program or employment agreement, up to the applicable tax-qualified plan
compensation limit ($230,000 in 2008). Final average earnings are the average
of the highest five consecutive years of earnings out of the last 10&nbsp;years
prior to the earlier of termination or December&nbsp;31, 2008. Participants
vest in their benefits after completing five years of service with us. The
normal retirement age is age 65, but participants who are age 55 with
10&nbsp;years of service may elect to retire early. Benefits are reduced by 6%
per year from age 65.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">110<a name="PB_110_165925_2897"></a></font></p>

<p align="left" style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">SIPP II</font></b></p>

<p align="left" style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SIPP II
was designed to provide a benefit to certain participants selected by the
Jefferson Smurfit Corporation Board of Directors.&#160; We have not admitted new participants into
this plan since 1998, and only two of our currently active officers are
participants, including Mr.&nbsp;Moore. Mr.&nbsp;Hinrichs&#146; employment
terminated May&nbsp;18, 2009 and he waived his claim to benefits under this
plan when he entered into a Confidential Non-Compete and Consulting Agreement
with us. Participants earn service for the period of employment with us. The
benefit formula is 2.5% of final average earnings multiplied by service limited
to 20&nbsp;years plus 1.0% of final average earnings multiplied by service in
excess of 20&nbsp;years minus 1.2% of the primary insurance amount multiplied
by service and less the benefit earned under the tax-qualified pension plan.
The portion of the benefit earned for service after December&nbsp;31, 2006
(before the tax-qualified offset) is adjusted by a fraction, the numerator of
which is the portion of the Universal tax-qualified benefit that would have
been earned for service after December&nbsp;31, 2006 if benefit accruals had
not ceased under the Universal Plan and the denominator of which is the
tax-qualified benefit that would have been earned for service after December&nbsp;31,
2006 if the JSC Pension Plan provisions had not been amended. Earnings are base
pay plus amounts earned under the MIP. Final average earnings are the average
of the highest five consecutive years of earnings out of the last 10&nbsp;years
prior to termination. Both of the current participants in this plan are vested
in their benefits. The normal retirement age is age 65, but participants who
are age 55 with five years of service may elect to retire early. The benefit is
reduced by 5% per year from age 65 if the participant has less than
10&nbsp;years of service at termination and from age 62 if the participant has
at least 10&nbsp;years of service. For the portion of the benefit earned for
service after December&nbsp;31, 2006, the early commencement factors are
applied to the respective benefits before the fractional adjustment described
above is made. The normal form of payment is a single-life annuity.
Participants were required to elect to receive their benefits in the form of a
lump-sum distribution or another optional form, which is actuarially
equivalent, by making a written election by December&nbsp;31, 2008.&#160; Mr.&nbsp;Moore elected the lump-sum
distribution.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">SIPP III</font></b></p>

<p align="left" style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SIPP III
restores benefits to participants whose compensation exceeds the applicable
tax-qualified plan compensation limits ($230,000 in 2008). The provisions of
SIPP III are the same as the relevant portion of the Pension Plan described
above, except earnings above the applicable tax-qualified plan compensation
limit are used. This SIPP III benefit is then offset by the Pension Plan
benefit. All benefit accruals ceased as of December&nbsp;31, 2008.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Executive Retirement Agreement with Mr.&nbsp;Klinger</font></b></p>

<p align="left" style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Klinger Retirement Agreement was designed to provide a target benefit to Mr.&nbsp;Klinger.
Service is earned while he is employed by us. The benefit formula is 50% of
final average earnings, less $30,678 and benefits earned under any Company
sponsored retirement plans, excluding accruals attributable to salary deferrals
and matching employer contributions. Earnings include basic salary and annual
incentive bonuses, but exclude compensation under long-term incentive plans and
any other bonus or incentive compensation. Final average earnings are the
average of the highest four consecutive years of earnings out of the last
10&nbsp;years prior to termination. Mr.&nbsp;Klinger is immediately vested in
his benefit. Prior to completing 15&nbsp;years of service with us, the benefit
will be prorated by the ratio of service at termination to 15. Mr.&nbsp;Klinger
is entitled to a full retirement benefit after completion of 15&nbsp;years of
service.&#160; Benefits commence on the first
day of the seventh month following termination, if he has completed at least
15&nbsp;years of service, or on the later of age 62 or the first day of the
seventh month following termination if he has not completed 15&nbsp;years of
service.&#160; The normal form of payment is a
single-life annuity. The value of the single-life annuity benefit is converted
and paid in five equal annual installments.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">111<a name="PB_111_165949_3020"></a></font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Non-Qualified
Deferred Compensation Table</font></b></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following table
discloses contributions, earnings and balances under our non-qualified deferred
compensation plan for Mr.&nbsp;Moore as of December&nbsp;31, 2009. This
non-qualified deferred compensation plan is no longer offered by us, and Mr.&nbsp;Moore
is the only NEO participating in the plan. He is no longer eligible to make
executive contributions to the plan, and we make no registrant contributions to
the plan. The only contributions made to this plan were employee contributions
of deferred bonus payments from 1991. Earnings in Mr.&nbsp;Moore&#146;s account
accrue on the basis of a fixed rate of interest tied to Moody&#146;s Corporate Bond
Yield Index plus 2%. The earnings represent an unfunded liability of ours.
Subject to the impact of our bankruptcy filing, Mr.&nbsp;Moore will be entitled
to receive the payout under this plan only upon retirement or other termination
of employment with us.</font></p>

Company and receives no additional compensation by reason of his membership on
or attendance at meetings of the Board of Directors.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">EMPLOYMENT
AGREEMENTS AND POST-TERMINATION PAYMENTS</font></b></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">The Employment Agreements of Messrs. Moore, Klinger and Hinrichs</font></b></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have entered into agreements (the Employment Agreements) with Messrs.&nbsp;Moore,
Klinger and</font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> Hinrichs. The Employment Agreements of Messrs.&nbsp;Moore
and Klinger and Mr. Klinger&#146;s Executive Retirement Agreement are expected to be
replaced by new agreements (the New Agreements) upon our emergence from
bankruptcy proceedings.&#160; Accordingly, the
following discussion will describe both the Employment Agreements and the New
Agreements.&#160; In connection with the
termination of his employment, Mr.&nbsp;Hinrichs entered into a Confidential
Non-Compete and Consulting Agreement.&#160; Mr.&nbsp;Hinrichs
waived all claims for any other payment under his Employment Agreement.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">The
Employment Agreements</font></b></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Employment Agreements require the executives to devote substantially
all of their business time to</font><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> our operations through the term of
each executive&#146;s respective Employment Agreement, unless sooner terminated by
either party in accordance with the provisions of such Employment Agreement.
The Employment Agreements provide that the executives shall be eligible to
participate in any annual performance bonus plans, long-term incentive plans,
and/or equity-based compensation plans established or maintained by us for our
senior executive officers, including the MIP and the LTIP.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Employment Agreements provide that if we terminate the executive&#146;s employment &#147;without
cause&#148; or the executive terminates his employment with &#147;good reason&#148;, we will: (i)&nbsp;pay
the executive the full amount of base salary and annual bonus that we would
have paid under the Employment Agreement had the executive&#146;s employment
continued to the end of the employment term; (ii)&nbsp;continue the executive&#146;s</font></p>

<p align="center" style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Arial" style="font-size:10.0pt;">112<a name="PB_112_170212_7748"></a></font></p>
